ko.R: 그러나 예수께서 다시 말씀하셨다. "얘들아, 하나님의 나라에 들어가기는 정말 어렵다!

es.L: Pero Jesús, respondiendo de nuevo, les dice: «Hijos, ¡qué difícil es entrar en el reino de Dios!
es.B: Pero Jesús les volvió a decir: «Hijos míos, ¡qué difícil es entrar en el reino de Dios!
es.R: Pero Jesús volvió a decir: «Hijos míos, ¡es muy difícil entrar en el reino de Dios!

fr.L: Mais Jésus, reprenant la parole, leur dit de nouveau : « Enfants, qu’il est difficile d’entrer dans le royaume de Dieu !
fr.B: Mais Jésus leur dit encore : « Mes enfants, qu’il est difficile d’entrer dans le royaume de Dieu !
fr.R: Mais Jésus a répété : « Mes enfants, c’est très difficile d’entrer dans le royaume de Dieu !

sw.L: Lakini Yesu anajibu tena, anawaambia, "Watoto, jinsi ilivyo vigumu kuingia katika ufalme wa Mungu!
sw.B: Lakini Yesu akawaambia tena, "Wanangu, ni vigumu kama nini kuingia katika ufalme wa Mungu!
sw.R: Lakini Yesu akasema tena, "Wanangu, ni vigumu sana kuingia katika ufalme wa Mungu!

pt.L: Mas Jesus, respondendo outra vez, lhes diz: "Filhos, como é difícil entrar no Reino de Deus!
pt.B: Mas Jesus lhes disse de novo: "Meus filhos, como é difícil entrar no Reino de Deus!
pt.R: Mas Jesus disse outra vez: "Meus filhos, é muito difícil entrar no Reino de Deus!

decisions.choice: children: a warm address to the disciples
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to grown men as a teacher or father speaks to his own. Only here in Mark does he call his disciples "children".

decisions.choice: how hard it is to enter: in the SBLGNT, said of everyone
alternatives: how hard it is for those who trust in riches to enter
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "for those who trust in riches", which limits the saying to the rich. The earliest lack it, and the shorter text is harder: it is hard for anyone to enter. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: answering says: speaks again in response
decisions.reason: The disciples have not spoken; Jesus responds to their astonishment.

decisions.choice: My children
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "my" to keep the warmth of the address.

decisions.choice: "Hỡi các con" (L); "Này các con" (B); "Các con ơi" (R) for "Children"
decisions.reason: As John 21:5: "các con" is already how Jesus speaks to his disciples, and the address keeps its warmth at every level.

decisions.choice: "자녀들아" (L); "얘들아" (B, R)
decisions.reason: A warm address to the disciples (meaning decision); Literal keeps the word "children", and Balanced and Readable use the affectionate address the Korean John uses at 21:5.

decisions.choice: Filhos (L); Meus filhos (B, R)
decisions.reason: Portuguese addresses grown people warmly as "filhos", as an older person or a teacher does; "Crianças" would sound as if he were talking to the children of 10:13, and "Filhinhos" is sentimental.

source.text: εὐκοπώτερόν ἐστιν κάμηλον διὰ τῆς τρυμαλιᾶς τῆς ῥαφίδος διελθεῖν ἢ πλούσιον εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελθεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Easier it is a camel through the eye of the needle to pass than a rich man into the kingdom of God to enter.

en.L: It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of the needle than for {{gender:a rich person|a rich man}} to enter into the kingdom of God."
en.B: A camel could pass through the eye of a needle more easily than a rich person could enter the kingdom of God."
en.R: A camel is a very big animal, and the hole in a needle is very small. But a camel could get through that hole more easily than a rich person could enter God's kingdom."

vi.L: Con lạc đà đi qua lỗ kim còn dễ hơn người giàu vào vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời."
vi.B: Một con lạc đà chui qua lỗ kim còn dễ hơn một người giàu vào được vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời."
vi.R: Lạc đà là một con vật rất lớn, còn lỗ kim thì rất nhỏ. Thế nhưng một con lạc đà chui qua lỗ kim còn dễ hơn một người giàu vào vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời."

ko.L: 낙타가 바늘귀로 지나가는 것이 부자가 하나님의 나라에 들어가는 것보다 더 쉽다."
ko.B: 부자가 하나님의 나라에 들어가는 것보다 낙타가 바늘귀로 지나가는 것이 더 쉽다."
ko.R: 낙타는 아주 큰 짐승이고, 바늘귀는 아주 작은 구멍이다. 그런데 부자가 하나님의 나라에 들어가는 것보다 낙타가 그 바늘귀로 빠져나가는 것이 더 쉽다."

es.L: Es más fácil para un camello pasar por el ojo de la aguja que para un rico entrar en el reino de Dios».
es.B: Es más fácil que un camello pase por el ojo de una aguja que un rico entre en el reino de Dios».
es.R: Un camello es un animal muy grande, y el agujero de una aguja es muy pequeño. Pero sería más fácil que un camello pasara por ese agujero que una persona rica entrara en el reino de Dios».

fr.L: Il est plus facile à un chameau de passer par le trou de l’aiguille qu’à un riche d’entrer dans le royaume de Dieu. »
fr.B: Un chameau passerait plus facilement par le trou d’une aiguille qu’un riche n’entrerait dans le royaume de Dieu. »
fr.R: Un chameau, c’est un très gros animal, et le trou d’une aiguille est tout petit. Mais un chameau passerait plus facilement par ce trou qu’un riche n’entrerait dans le royaume de Dieu. »

sw.L: Ni rahisi zaidi kwa ngamia kupita katika tundu la sindano, kuliko kwa tajiri kuingia katika ufalme wa Mungu."
sw.B: Ngamia angepita katika tundu la sindano kwa urahisi zaidi kuliko mtu tajiri angeweza kuingia katika ufalme wa Mungu."
sw.R: Ngamia ni mnyama mkubwa sana, na tundu la sindano ni dogo sana. Lakini ingekuwa rahisi zaidi kwa ngamia kupita katika tundu hilo kuliko kwa tajiri kuingia katika ufalme wa Mungu."

pt.L: É mais fácil um camelo passar pelo buraco da agulha do que um rico entrar no Reino de Deus."
pt.B: Um camelo passaria pelo buraco de uma agulha com mais facilidade do que um rico entraria no Reino de Deus."
pt.R: O camelo é um animal muito grande, e o buraco de uma agulha é muito pequeno. Mas seria mais fácil um camelo passar por esse buraco do que uma pessoa rica entrar no Reino de Deus."

decisions.choice: a camel through the eye of a needle: something impossible
alternatives: a small gate in Jerusalem called the needle
decisions.reason: The largest animal in the land and the smallest opening make a picture of what cannot happen. There is no early evidence for a gate called the needle's eye; that idea came much later. 10:27 shows that Jesus means it is impossible for people.

decisions.choice: camel
decisions.reason: A few late manuscripts read a similar Greek word meaning a ship's rope, which softens the picture. The SBLGNT and nearly all manuscripts read "camel". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: a rich man: anyone who is rich
decisions.reason: The word is masculine in form but speaks of rich people in general.

decisions.choice: A camel is a very big animal, and the hole in a needle is very small
alternatives: a camel through the eye of the needle
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture so that young readers see the point.

decisions.choice: "người giàu" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese word already means any rich person, so the English gender span has no Vietnamese counterpart.

decisions.choice: "부자" with no gender span
decisions.reason: "부자" already means any rich person, man or woman, so the gender setting has nothing to change (style guide, section 7).

decisions.choice: un rico (L, B); una persona rica (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish "un rico" already means anyone who is rich (meaning decision), so no gender setting is needed where the English Literal has one.

decisions.choice: un riche (L), with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span such as un riche / un homme riche
decisions.reason: The Greek has the adjective "rich" alone. French "un riche" says it the same way and already means any rich person, so no gender setting is needed where the English Literal has one.

decisions.choice: um rico, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: Portuguese can use the adjective as a noun, "um rico", which means any rich person, as in Matthew 19:24, so the choice the English setting offers between "person" and "man" does not arise (m3).

source.text: οἱ δὲ περισσῶς ἐξεπλήσσοντο λέγοντες πρὸς ἑαυτούς· Καὶ τίς δύναται σωθῆναι;

records.literal_gloss: And exceedingly they were astonished saying to themselves, And who is able to be saved?

en.L: And they were exceedingly astonished, saying to one another, "Then who can be saved?"
en.B: They were utterly amazed and said to each other, "Who can be saved, then?"
en.R: The followers were even more surprised. They said to each other, "Then who can be saved?"

vi.L: Và họ hết sức kinh ngạc, nói với nhau: "Vậy thì ai có thể được cứu?"
vi.B: Các môn đồ vô cùng kinh ngạc và nói với nhau: "Vậy thì ai có thể được cứu?"
vi.R: Các môn đồ lại càng ngạc nhiên hơn nữa. Họ nói với nhau: "Thế thì ai có thể được cứu?"

ko.L: 그러자 그들은 더욱 몹시 놀라서 서로 말했다. "그러면 누가 구원받을 수 있는가?"
ko.B: 제자들은 더욱 크게 놀라서 서로 말했다. "그렇다면 누가 구원받을 수 있겠는가?"
ko.R: 제자들은 더욱더 놀랐다. 그래서 서로 말했다. "그러면 누가 구원받을 수 있겠느냐?"

es.L: Y ellos se asombraban sobremanera, diciendo entre sí: «¿Y quién puede ser salvo?».
es.B: Ellos se quedaron aún más asombrados y se decían unos a otros: «Entonces, ¿quién puede salvarse?».
es.R: Los discípulos se sorprendieron todavía más. Se decían unos a otros: «Entonces, ¿quién puede salvarse?».

fr.L: Et ils étaient extrêmement stupéfaits, se disant les uns aux autres : « Et qui peut être sauvé ? »
fr.B: Ils furent profondément stupéfaits et se dirent entre eux : « Mais alors, qui peut être sauvé ? »
fr.R: Les disciples ont été encore plus surpris. Ils se disaient entre eux : « Alors, qui peut être sauvé ? »

sw.L: Nao wakashangaa kupita kiasi, wakiambiana wao kwa wao, "Basi, ni nani anayeweza kuokolewa?"
sw.B: Walishangaa sana, wakaulizana, "Kama ndivyo, ni nani basi atakayeokolewa?"
sw.R: Wanafunzi walishangaa zaidi. Wakaambiana, "Basi ni nani anayeweza kuokolewa?"

pt.L: E eles ficaram extremamente espantados, dizendo uns aos outros: "Então quem pode ser salvo?"
pt.B: Eles ficaram muito admirados e diziam uns aos outros: "Quem pode ser salvo, então?"
pt.R: Os seguidores ficaram ainda mais surpresos. Eles disseram uns aos outros: "Então quem pode ser salvo?"

decisions.choice: be saved: be rescued by God and given life in his kingdom
decisions.reason: Here being saved means the same as entering the kingdom and inheriting eternal life (10:17, 23).

decisions.choice: then: if even the rich cannot, who can
decisions.reason: The word draws a conclusion from what Jesus said.

decisions.choice: saying to one another
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "saying to him", so that the disciples ask Jesus. The SBLGNT reads "to themselves", that is, to one another. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: The followers were even more surprised
decisions.reason: Readable names who was amazed and links this to 10:24.

decisions.choice: "구원받다"
decisions.reason: To be saved is to be rescued by God and given life in his kingdom (meaning decision); "구원" is the word of the Korean John (10:9; 12:47). The disciples speak among themselves in the plain style.

source.text: ἐμβλέψας αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει· Παρὰ ἀνθρώποις ἀδύνατον ἀλλ’ οὐ παρὰ θεῷ, πάντα γὰρ δυνατὰ παρὰ τῷ θεῷ.

records.literal_gloss: Having looked at them Jesus says, With men impossible, but not with God; all things for possible with God.

en.L: Looking at them, Jesus says, "With {{gender:people|men}} [it is] impossible, but not with God; for all things are possible with God."
en.B: Jesus looked straight at them and said, "For human beings it cannot be done, but not for God. God can do anything."
en.R: Jesus looked at them and said, "People cannot do this. But God can. God can do everything."

vi.L: Nhìn họ, Đức Giê-xu nói: "Đối với loài người, [điều đó là] không thể, nhưng đối với Đức Chúa Trời thì không; vì đối với Đức Chúa Trời mọi sự đều có thể."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nhìn thẳng vào họ và nói: "Đối với loài người thì không thể được, nhưng đối với Đức Chúa Trời thì không phải vậy. Đức Chúa Trời làm được mọi sự."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nhìn họ và nói: "Con người không thể làm được điều này. Nhưng Đức Chúa Trời thì làm được. Đức Chúa Trời làm được mọi việc."

ko.L: 예수께서 그들을 바라보시며 말씀하신다. "사람에게는 불가능하지만 하나님께는 그렇지 않다. 하나님께는 모든 것이 가능하기 때문이다."
ko.B: 예수께서 그들을 똑바로 바라보시며 말씀하셨다. "사람은 할 수 없지만, 하나님은 그렇지 않으시다. 하나님께서는 무엇이든 하실 수 있다."
ko.R: 예수께서 그들을 바라보시며 말씀하셨다. "사람은 이 일을 할 수 없다. 그러나 하나님은 하실 수 있다. 하나님께서는 모든 것을 하실 수 있다."

es.L: Mirándolos, Jesús dice: «Para {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}} [es] imposible, pero no para Dios; porque todo es posible para Dios».
es.B: Jesús los miró fijamente y dijo: «Para los seres humanos es imposible, pero no para Dios. Dios lo puede todo».
es.R: Jesús los miró y dijo: «La gente no puede hacer esto. Pero Dios sí puede. Dios puede hacer todas las cosas».

fr.L: Les ayant regardés, Jésus dit : « Pour {{gender:les humains|les hommes}}, [c’est] impossible, mais non pour Dieu ; car tout est possible pour Dieu. »
fr.B: Jésus les regarda en face et dit : « Pour les êtres humains, c’est impossible, mais pas pour Dieu. Dieu peut tout faire. »
fr.R: Jésus les a regardés et a dit : « Les gens ne peuvent pas faire cela. Mais Dieu, lui, le peut. Dieu peut tout faire. »

sw.L: Yesu akiwatazama, anasema, "Kwa wanadamu [jambo hili] haliwezekani, lakini si kwa Mungu; kwa maana mambo yote yanawezekana kwa Mungu."
sw.B: Yesu akawatazama moja kwa moja, akasema, "Kwa wanadamu jambo hili haliwezekani, lakini kwa Mungu sivyo. Mungu anaweza kufanya lolote."
sw.R: Yesu akawatazama, akasema, "Watu hawawezi kufanya hivyo. Lakini Mungu anaweza. Mungu anaweza kufanya kila kitu."

pt.L: Olhando para eles, Jesus diz: "Para {{gender:os seres humanos|os homens}} [é] impossível, mas não para Deus; pois todas as coisas são possíveis para Deus."
pt.B: Jesus olhou bem para eles e disse: "Para os seres humanos isso não é possível, mas para Deus é. Deus pode fazer tudo."
pt.R: Jesus olhou para eles e disse: "As pessoas não conseguem fazer isso. Mas Deus consegue. Deus pode fazer todas as coisas."

decisions.choice: all things are possible with God: the faith of Israel's Scriptures
decisions.reason: The words recall Genesis 18:14, "Is anything too hard for the LORD?", said when Sarah was promised a son, and Job 42:2.

decisions.choice: impossible with people, not with God: salvation is God's work
alternatives: the rich can save themselves with effort
decisions.reason: No one, rich or poor, can enter by human power. God alone can bring them in.

decisions.choice: says: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: God can do anything (B); God can do everything (R)
alternatives: all things are possible with God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say the same thing with God as the subject.

decisions.choice: "loài người" (L, B), "con người" (R) with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese words already mean human beings.

decisions.choice: "사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: "사람" already includes men and women; the English span has nothing to match in Korean (style guide, section 7).

source.text: Ἤρξατο λέγειν ὁ Πέτρος αὐτῷ· Ἰδοὺ ἡμεῖς ἀφήκαμεν πάντα καὶ ἠκολουθήκαμέν σοι.

records.literal_gloss: Began to say Peter to him, Behold, we have left all and have followed you.

en.L: Peter began to say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Look, we have left everything and have followed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.B: Peter spoke up: "Look, we have left everything behind to follow {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.R: Then Peter said to Jesus, "Look at us! We have left everything we had, and we have followed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

vi.L: Phi-e-rơ bắt đầu nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Này, chúng con đã bỏ mọi sự và đã đi theo Thầy."
vi.B: Phi-e-rơ lên tiếng thưa: "Thầy xem, chúng con đã bỏ hết mọi sự để theo Thầy."
vi.R: Rồi Phi-e-rơ thưa với Đức Giê-xu: "Thầy nhìn chúng con đây! Chúng con đã bỏ hết mọi thứ mình có, và chúng con đã đi theo Thầy."

ko.L: 베드로가 그분께 말하기 시작했다. "보십시오, 저희는 모든 것을 버리고 선생님을 따랐습니다."
ko.B: 베드로가 나서서 말했다. "보십시오, 저희는 모든 것을 버리고 선생님을 따랐습니다."
ko.R: 그러자 베드로가 예수께 말했다. "저희를 보십시오! 저희는 가진 것을 다 버리고 선생님을 따라왔습니다."

es.L: Pedro comenzó a decirle: «Mira, nosotros lo hemos dejado todo y {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} hemos seguido».
es.B: Pedro {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Mira, nosotros hemos dejado todo para seguirte».
es.R: Entonces Pedro {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo a Jesús: «¡Míranos! Hemos dejado todo lo que teníamos y {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} hemos seguido».

fr.L: Pierre se mit à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dire : « Regarde : nous avons tout quitté et nous {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}avons suivi. »
fr.B: Pierre prit la parole : « Tu vois, nous avons tout laissé pour {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} suivre. »
fr.R: Alors Pierre a dit à Jésus : « Regarde-nous ! Nous avons quitté tout ce que nous avions, et nous {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}avons suivi. »

sw.L: Petro akaanza kumwambia, "Angalia, sisi tumeviacha vitu vyote, na tumekufuata {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}."
sw.B: Petro akasema, "Angalia, sisi tumeacha kila kitu ili tukufuate!"
sw.R: Kisha Petro akamwambia Yesu, "Tuangalie sisi! Tumeacha kila kitu tulichokuwa nacho, na tumekufuata."

pt.L: Pedro começou a {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} dizer: "Eis que nós deixamos tudo e {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} seguimos."
pt.B: Pedro tomou a palavra: "Olha, nós deixamos tudo para trás para {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} seguir."
pt.R: Então Pedro disse a Jesus: "Olha para nós! Nós deixamos tudo o que tínhamos e {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} seguimos."

decisions.choice: have left, have followed: perfects, a step taken that still holds
decisions.reason: The tense shows a decision made in the past that continues. Peter contrasts the disciples with the rich man.

decisions.choice: look: calls attention to what follows
decisions.reason: The word draws attention to what Peter is about to say.

decisions.choice: we have left everything: as Peter and Andrew left their nets (1:18)
decisions.reason: James and John left their father in the boat (1:20) and Levi left his tax booth (2:14).

decisions.choice: "chúng con" and "Thầy" in the disciples' words, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As in John and Mark 9: the disciples speak to Jesus as their teacher; the same in 10:35-39.

decisions.choice: Olha (B); Olha para nós (R)
decisions.reason: Peter speaks to Jesus, so the word that calls attention takes the "tu" imperative, "Olha", not the "você" form "Olhe" (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4). Literal keeps "Eis que", as Matthew 19:27 does.

source.text: ἔφη ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐδείς ἐστιν ὃς ἀφῆκεν οἰκίαν ἢ ἀδελφοὺς ἢ ἀδελφὰς ἢ μητέρα ἢ πατέρα ἢ τέκνα ἢ ἀγροὺς ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ καὶ ἕνεκεν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, ἐὰν μὴ λάβῃ ἑκατονταπλασίονα νῦν ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τούτῳ οἰκίας καὶ ἀδελφοὺς καὶ ἀδελφὰς καὶ μητέρας καὶ τέκνα καὶ ἀγροὺς μετὰ διωγμῶν, καὶ ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τῷ ἐρχομένῳ ζωὴν αἰώνιον.

records.literal_gloss: Was saying Jesus, Truly I say to you, no one there is who has left house or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or lands for the sake of me and for the sake of the gospel, \v 30 if not he shall receive a hundredfold now in the time this, houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and lands, with persecutions, and in the age the coming life eternal.

en.L: Jesus said, "Truly I say to you, there is no one who has left house or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or fields for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sake and for the sake of the gospel \v 30 who will not receive a hundredfold now in this time, houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, with persecutions, and in the age to come eternal life.
en.B: Jesus said, "Truly I tell you, anyone who has left a home, brothers or sisters, mother or father, children or land because of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and because of the gospel \v 30 will receive a hundred times as much now, in this present time: homes, brothers, sisters, mothers, children and land, together with persecutions. And in the age that is coming they will receive eternal life.
en.R: Jesus said, "I tell you the truth: some people have left their homes, brothers, sisters, mother, father, children or farms because of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and the good news. \v 30 Every one of them will get a hundred times as much in this life. They will have homes, brothers, sisters, mothers, children and farms. People will also treat them cruelly for following {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. And in the world to come they will have eternal life.

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu nói: "Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, không có ai đã bỏ nhà cửa, hoặc anh em, hoặc chị em, hoặc mẹ, hoặc cha, hoặc con cái, hoặc ruộng đất vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và vì Tin Lành, \v 30 mà không nhận được gấp trăm lần ngay bây giờ trong đời này: nhà cửa, anh em, chị em, mẹ, con cái và ruộng đất, cùng với sự bắt bớ, và trong đời sắp đến thì [nhận được] sự sống đời đời.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nói: "Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, ai đã bỏ nhà cửa, anh em, chị em, mẹ, cha, con cái hay ruộng đất vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và vì Tin Lành, \v 30 thì ngay trong đời này sẽ nhận được gấp trăm lần: nhà cửa, anh em, chị em, mẹ, con cái và ruộng đất, cùng với sự bắt bớ. Và trong đời sắp đến, người ấy sẽ nhận được sự sống đời đời.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói: "Ta nói thật với các con: có những người đã bỏ nhà cửa, anh em, chị em, mẹ, cha, con cái hay ruộng vườn vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và vì Tin Lành. \v 30 Mỗi người trong họ sẽ nhận lại gấp trăm lần ngay trong đời này. Họ sẽ có nhà cửa, anh em, chị em, mẹ, con cái và ruộng vườn. Người ta cũng sẽ bắt bớ họ vì họ theo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Và trong đời sắp đến, họ sẽ có sự sống đời đời.

ko.L: 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "진실로 너희에게 말한다. 나 때문에, 그리고 복음 때문에 집이나 형제나 자매나 어머니나 아버지나 자녀나 밭을 버린 사람은, \v 30 지금 이 시대에 집과 형제와 자매와 어머니와 자녀와 밭을 박해와 함께 백 배나 받고, 오는 세상에서는 영원한 생명을 받지 않는 사람이 없다.
ko.B: 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "진실로 너희에게 말한다. 나 때문에, 그리고 복음 때문에 집이나 형제나 자매나 어머니나 아버지나 자녀나 밭을 버린 사람은, \v 30 지금 이 세상에서 집과 형제와 자매와 어머니와 자녀와 밭을 백 배나 받을 것이다. 박해도 함께 받을 것이다. 그리고 오는 세상에서는 영원한 생명을 받을 것이다.
ko.R: 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "내가 분명히 말한다. 나 때문에, 그리고 기쁜 소식 때문에 자기 집이나 형제나 자매나 어머니나 아버지나 자녀나 농토를 떠난 사람들이 있다. \v 30 그런 사람은 누구나 이 세상에서 백 배나 받을 것이다. 집과 형제와 자매와 어머니와 자녀와 농토를 얻게 될 것이다. 또 나를 따른다는 이유로 사람들에게 괴롭힘도 당할 것이다. 그리고 앞으로 올 세상에서는 영원한 생명을 얻을 것이다.

es.L: Jesús dijo: «En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que no hay nadie que haya dejado casa, o hermanos, o hermanas, o madre, o padre, o hijos, o campos por causa de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y por causa del evangelio, \v 30 que no reciba cien veces más ahora en este tiempo, casas y hermanos y hermanas y madres e hijos y campos, con persecuciones, y en la era venidera, vida eterna.
es.B: Jesús dijo: «En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que todo el que haya dejado casa, hermanos o hermanas, madre o padre, hijos o tierras por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y por el evangelio \v 30 recibirá cien veces más ahora, en este tiempo: casas, hermanos, hermanas, madres, hijos y tierras, junto con persecuciones. Y en la era venidera recibirá la vida eterna.
es.R: Jesús dijo: «{{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: algunas personas han dejado su casa, sus hermanos, sus hermanas, su madre, su padre, sus hijos o sus tierras por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y por la buena noticia. \v 30 Cada una de ellas recibirá cien veces más en esta vida. Tendrán casas, hermanos, hermanas, madres, hijos y tierras. La gente también las tratará con crueldad por seguirme. Y en el mundo que viene tendrán la vida eterna.

fr.L: Jésus dit : « En vérité, je vous le dis, il n’y a personne qui ait quitté maison, ou frères, ou sœurs, ou mère, ou père, ou enfants, ou champs à cause de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et à cause de l’Évangile, \v 30 qui ne reçoive au centuple maintenant, en ce temps-ci, maisons, et frères, et sœurs, et mères, et enfants, et champs, avec des persécutions, et, dans l’âge qui vient, la vie éternelle.
fr.B: Jésus répondit : « En vérité, je vous le dis : quiconque aura quitté maison, frères ou sœurs, mère ou père, enfants ou terres à cause de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et à cause de l’Évangile \v 30 recevra cent fois plus dès maintenant, en ce temps présent : des maisons, des frères, des sœurs, des mères, des enfants et des terres, avec des persécutions. Et dans le monde qui vient, il recevra la vie éternelle.
fr.R: Jésus a dit : « Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité : certaines personnes ont quitté leur maison, leurs frères, leurs sœurs, leur mère, leur père, leurs enfants ou leurs champs à cause de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et de la bonne nouvelle. \v 30 Chacune d’elles recevra cent fois plus dans cette vie. Elles auront des maisons, des frères, des sœurs, des mères, des enfants et des champs. Les gens les maltraiteront aussi parce qu’elles {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} suivent. Et dans le monde à venir, elles auront la vie éternelle.

sw.L: Yesu akasema, "Kweli nawaambia, hakuna mtu aliyeacha nyumba, au ndugu wa kiume, au ndugu wa kike, au mama, au baba, au watoto, au mashamba, kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na kwa ajili ya Injili, \v 30 ambaye hatapokea mara mia sasa katika wakati huu: nyumba, na ndugu wa kiume, na ndugu wa kike, na mama, na watoto, na mashamba, pamoja na mateso, na katika enzi ijayo uzima wa milele.
sw.B: Yesu akasema, "Kweli nawaambia, mtu yeyote aliyeacha nyumba, kaka au dada, mama au baba, watoto au mashamba kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na kwa ajili ya Injili, \v 30 atapokea mara mia zaidi sasa katika wakati huu wa sasa: nyumba, kaka, dada, akina mama, watoto na mashamba, pamoja na mateso. Na katika enzi inayokuja atapokea uzima wa milele.
sw.R: Yesu akasema, "Nawaambia ukweli: kuna watu walioacha nyumba zao, kaka, dada, mama, baba, watoto au mashamba kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na kwa ajili ya Habari Njema. \v 30 Kila mmoja wao atapata mara mia zaidi katika maisha haya. Watakuwa na nyumba, kaka, dada, akina mama, watoto na mashamba. Watu watawatesa pia kwa sababu ya kunifuata. Na katika ulimwengu ujao watapata uzima wa milele.

pt.L: Jesus disse: "Em verdade eu lhes digo: não há ninguém que tenha deixado casa, ou irmãos, ou irmãs, ou mãe, ou pai, ou filhos, ou campos por causa de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} e por causa do evangelho \v 30 que não receba cem vezes mais agora, neste tempo, casas, e irmãos, e irmãs, e mães, e filhos, e campos, com perseguições, e, na era que vem, a vida eterna.
pt.B: Jesus disse: "Em verdade eu lhes digo: quem deixou casa, irmãos ou irmãs, mãe ou pai, filhos ou terras por causa de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} e por causa do evangelho \v 30 vai receber cem vezes mais agora, no tempo presente: casas, irmãos, irmãs, mães, filhos e terras, junto com perseguições. E, na era que está por vir, receberá a vida eterna.
pt.R: Jesus disse: "Eu garanto a vocês: algumas pessoas deixaram a sua casa, os seus irmãos, as suas irmãs, a mãe, o pai, os filhos ou as suas terras por causa de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} e das boas-novas. \v 30 Cada uma delas vai receber cem vezes mais nesta vida. Vão ter casas, irmãos, irmãs, mães, filhos e terras. As pessoas também vão maltratá-las porque elas {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} seguem. E, no mundo que vai vir, elas vão ter a vida eterna.

decisions.choice: a hundredfold now: a new family and shared homes among Jesus' followers
alternatives: great personal wealth in this life
decisions.reason: Jesus has already called those who do God's will his brother and sister and mother (3:34-35). Those who leave family find a far larger family among his followers, who share their homes.

decisions.choice: mothers, but not fathers: the second list leaves out fathers
decisions.reason: The new family has mothers, but Jesus does not name fathers. It may be because God alone is Father in this family (11:25; Matthew 23:9). Mark does not explain.

decisions.choice: persecutions: harassment and suffering for following Jesus
decisions.reason: Jesus does not promise ease. The gift of the new family comes with suffering, as in 4:17 and 13:9-13.

decisions.choice: the age to come, eternal life: the life of God's coming age
decisions.reason: Jews spoke of this age and the age to come. Eternal life belongs to the age to come, and it answers the man's question in 10:17.

decisions.choice: mother or father: the SBLGNT list has no wife
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts add "or wife" to the first list, as in Luke 18:29. The earliest lack it. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: no one who ... who will not receive: everyone who has left will receive
decisions.reason: The double negative makes a firm promise to all who have left these things.

decisions.choice: anyone who has left ... will receive (B); some people have left ... Every one of them will get (R)
alternatives: there is no one who has left ... who will not receive
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the double negative into a positive promise. Readable splits the long sentence and says what persecutions are.

decisions.choice: "Tin Lành" for the gospel, at every level
decisions.reason: As in Colossians. The Protestant word already means "good news", so Readable needs no other word where the English Readable says "good news".

decisions.choice: "đời sắp đến" for "the age to come"
decisions.reason: "đời sau" would suggest only life after death; "đời sắp đến" keeps the coming age of God, set against "đời này" (this time).

decisions.choice: "복음" (L, B); "기쁜 소식" (R)
decisions.reason: Key term: "gospel" at Literal and Balanced, "good news" at Readable, as the English does and as the Korean Colossians does (1:23).

decisions.choice: the double negative "no one ... who will not receive" is kept at the end of the sentence
decisions.reason: Korean can keep the Greek's "there is no one who ... does not receive" only by putting "없다" last; Balanced and Readable say it positively, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "박해" (L, B); "괴롭힘을 당하다" (R)
decisions.reason: "박해" is the word of the Korean John (15:20); "핍박" is the older church word. Readable uses the everyday word.

decisions.choice: evangelio (L, B); buena noticia (R)
decisions.reason: As the English key term does: Literal and Balanced say "evangelio"; Readable says "buena noticia", as the Spanish of 1 Peter does.

decisions.choice: hijos
decisions.reason: Spanish "hijos" means children of either sex, so it renders the Greek word for children directly.

decisions.choice: l’Évangile (L, B); la bonne nouvelle (R)
alternatives: la bonne nouvelle at every level
decisions.reason: As the other French books (Colossians, Ephesians, 1 Peter): the key term is "Évangile" at Literal and Balanced and "bonne nouvelle" at Readable, as the English says "gospel" and "good news".

decisions.choice: ndugu wa kiume, ndugu wa kike (L); kaka, dada (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek names brothers and sisters separately. "Ndugu" alone covers both, so Literal says "ndugu wa kiume" and "ndugu wa kike"; Balanced and Readable use the everyday "kaka" and "dada". No gender setting is involved: both are named.

decisions.choice: Injili (L, B); Habari Njema (R); enzi ijayo (L, B), ulimwengu ujao (R)
decisions.reason: As in the letters, the gospel is "Injili" at Literal and Balanced and "Habari Njema" at Readable. "Enzi" is an age or era; "kizazi" would say a generation of people. Readable says "the world to come", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: na era que vem (L); na era que está por vir (B)
decisions.reason: "Século" in this sense is archaic, and Brazilian readers take it as a hundred years. "Era" keeps the contrast between this time and the age to come (m4); Readable says "no mundo que vai vir", as the English Readable says "the world to come".

source.text: πολλοὶ δὲ ἔσονται πρῶτοι ἔσχατοι καὶ οἱ ἔσχατοι πρῶτοι.

records.literal_gloss: Many however will be first last and the last first.

en.L: But many [who are] first will be last, and the last first."
en.B: Yet many who are first will end up last, and the last first."
en.R: But many people who are important now will be the least important then. And many who are the least important now will be the most important."

vi.L: Nhưng nhiều người đứng đầu sẽ thành người cuối cùng, và những người cuối cùng [sẽ thành] người đứng đầu."
vi.B: Nhưng nhiều người đang đứng đầu sẽ trở thành người cuối cùng, và những người cuối cùng sẽ được đứng đầu."
vi.R: Nhưng nhiều người bây giờ đang quan trọng thì khi ấy sẽ trở thành kém quan trọng nhất. Và nhiều người bây giờ kém quan trọng nhất thì khi ấy sẽ trở thành quan trọng nhất."

ko.L: 그러나 첫째인 많은 사람이 꼴찌가 되고, 꼴찌인 [많은 사람이] 첫째가 될 것이다."
ko.B: 그러나 첫째인 많은 사람이 꼴찌가 되고, 꼴찌인 많은 사람이 첫째가 될 것이다."
ko.R: 그러나 지금 높은 사람들 가운데 많은 사람이 그때에는 가장 낮아질 것이다. 그리고 지금 가장 낮은 사람들 가운데 많은 사람이 그때에는 가장 높아질 것이다."

es.L: Pero muchos primeros serán últimos, y los últimos, primeros».
es.B: Sin embargo, muchos que ahora son primeros serán últimos, y los últimos serán primeros».
es.R: Pero muchas personas que ahora son importantes serán las menos importantes. Y muchas que ahora son las menos importantes serán las más importantes».

fr.L: Mais beaucoup [qui sont] premiers seront derniers, et les derniers premiers. »
fr.B: Pourtant, beaucoup de ceux qui sont les premiers seront les derniers, et les derniers seront les premiers. »
fr.R: Mais beaucoup de gens qui sont importants maintenant seront les moins importants plus tard. Et beaucoup de ceux qui sont les moins importants maintenant seront les plus importants. »

sw.L: Lakini wengi wa kwanza watakuwa wa mwisho, na wale wa mwisho [watakuwa] wa kwanza."
sw.B: Hata hivyo, wengi walio wa kwanza sasa wataishia kuwa wa mwisho, na walio wa mwisho watakuwa wa kwanza."
sw.R: Lakini watu wengi walio muhimu sasa watakuwa wa chini kabisa wakati ule. Na wengi walio wa chini kabisa sasa watakuwa muhimu kuliko wote."

pt.L: Mas muitos [que são] primeiros serão últimos, e os últimos, primeiros."
pt.B: Mas muitos que são os primeiros vão acabar sendo os últimos, e os últimos, os primeiros."
pt.R: Mas muitas pessoas que agora são importantes vão ser as menos importantes naquele tempo. E muitas que agora são as menos importantes vão ser as mais importantes."

decisions.choice: first and last: God reverses human ranking
alternatives: a rule about lines or order
decisions.reason: Those honored now, like the rich, may be last in the kingdom, and those who gave up everything may be first. The saying may also warn the disciples not to count on their own place.

decisions.choice: first last: the first will be last
decisions.reason: The verb "will be" links each pair: the first become last, the last become first.

decisions.choice: important now ... least important then
decisions.reason: Readable says what first and last mean and when the change comes.

decisions.choice: [많은 사람이]
decisions.reason: The Greek says "many" once for both halves; Korean repeats it in the second half, so Literal brackets the repetition.

source.text: Ἦσαν δὲ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ἀναβαίνοντες εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, καὶ ἦν προάγων αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἐθαμβοῦντο, οἱ δὲ ἀκολουθοῦντες ἐφοβοῦντο.

records.literal_gloss: They were then on the road going up to Jerusalem, and was going on before them Jesus, and they were astonished, and those following were afraid.

en.L: And they were on the road going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was going ahead of them, and they were astonished, and those who followed were afraid.
en.B: They were on the road going up to Jerusalem, with Jesus going on ahead of them. The disciples were astonished, and the others who followed were afraid.
en.R: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers were on the road going up to Jerusalem. Jesus was walking out in front of them. The disciples were amazed at this. The others who were following were afraid.

vi.L: Bấy giờ họ đang trên đường đi lên Giê-ru-sa-lem, và Đức Giê-xu đi trước họ; họ kinh ngạc, còn những người đi theo thì sợ hãi.
vi.B: Họ đang trên đường đi lên Giê-ru-sa-lem, và Đức Giê-xu đi trước họ. Các môn đồ kinh ngạc, còn những người khác đi theo thì sợ hãi.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu và các môn đồ đang trên đường đi lên Giê-ru-sa-lem. Đức Giê-xu đi phía trước họ. Các môn đồ rất ngạc nhiên về điều đó. Những người khác đi theo thì sợ hãi.

ko.L: 그들은 예루살렘으로 올라가는 길에 있었다. 그리고 예수께서 그들보다 앞서 가고 계셨다. 그러자 그들은 놀랐고, 따라오는 사람들은 두려워했다.
ko.B: 그들은 예루살렘으로 올라가는 길에 있었다. 예수께서는 그들보다 앞장서서 가고 계셨다. 제자들은 놀랐고, 뒤따르는 다른 사람들은 두려워했다.
ko.R: 예수와 제자들은 예루살렘으로 올라가는 길에 있었다. 예수께서는 그들 앞에서 앞장서 걸어가셨다. 제자들은 그것을 보고 놀랐다. 뒤따라오던 다른 사람들은 두려워했다.

es.L: E iban por el camino subiendo a Jerusalén, y Jesús iba delante de ellos, y ellos se asombraban, y los que [{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}] seguían tenían miedo.
es.B: Iban por el camino, subiendo a Jerusalén, y Jesús caminaba delante de ellos. Los discípulos estaban asombrados, y los demás que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} seguían tenían miedo.
es.R: Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos iban por el camino que sube a Jerusalén. Jesús caminaba delante de ellos. Los discípulos estaban asombrados por esto. Los otros que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} seguían tenían miedo.

fr.L: Or ils étaient en chemin, montant à Jérusalem, et Jésus allait devant eux, et ils étaient stupéfaits, et ceux qui suivaient avaient peur.
fr.B: Ils étaient en route pour monter à Jérusalem, et Jésus marchait devant eux. Les disciples étaient stupéfaits, et les autres qui suivaient avaient peur.
fr.R: Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples étaient sur la route qui monte à Jérusalem. Jésus marchait devant eux. Les disciples en étaient très étonnés. Les autres qui les suivaient avaient peur.

sw.L: Nao walikuwa njiani wakipanda kwenda Yerusalemu, na Yesu alikuwa akiwatangulia, nao walikuwa wakishangaa, na wale waliokuwa wakifuata waliogopa.
sw.B: Walikuwa njiani wakipanda kwenda Yerusalemu, na Yesu alikuwa akiwatangulia. Wanafunzi walishangaa, na wengine waliokuwa wakifuata waliogopa.
sw.R: Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikuwa njiani wakipanda kwenda Yerusalemu. Yesu alikuwa akitembea mbele yao. Wanafunzi walishangaa jambo hilo, na wale wengine waliokuwa wakifuata waliogopa.

pt.L: E estavam no caminho, subindo para Jerusalém, e Jesus ia à frente deles, e eles estavam assombrados, e os que [o] seguiam tinham medo.
pt.B: Eles estavam na estrada, subindo para Jerusalém, e Jesus ia à frente deles. Os discípulos estavam assombrados, e os outros que os seguiam tinham medo.
pt.R: Jesus e os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} seguidores estavam na estrada, subindo para Jerusalém. Jesus ia andando na frente deles. Os discípulos ficaram admirados com isso. Os outros que vinham atrás estavam com medo.

decisions.choice: going up to Jerusalem: Jerusalem stands high in the hills
decisions.reason: Travelers always went up to Jerusalem, which lies high in the hills of Judea. Pilgrims coming to the Passover took the road from Jericho (10:46).

decisions.choice: they were astonished, those who followed were afraid: perhaps two groups
alternatives: one group, the disciples, both amazed and afraid
decisions.reason: Mark may mean the disciples were amazed while others in the crowd following were afraid. He may also be describing the same people in two ways.

decisions.choice: Jesus was going ahead of them: he leads the way to his suffering
alternatives: he was walking alone by chance
decisions.reason: Jesus walks in front, knowing what waits in Jerusalem (8:31; 9:31). His resolve amazes and frightens those behind him.

decisions.choice: The disciples ... the others who followed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the two groups as Mark seems to mean them. This follows the more likely reading.

source.text: καὶ παραλαβὼν πάλιν τοὺς δώδεκα ἤρξατο αὐτοῖς λέγειν τὰ μέλλοντα αὐτῷ συμβαίνειν ὅτι Ἰδοὺ ἀναβαίνομεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδοθήσεται τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ τοῖς γραμματεῦσιν, καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτὸν θανάτῳ καὶ παραδώσουσιν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν καὶ ἐμπαίξουσιν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐμπτύσουσιν αὐτῷ καὶ μαστιγώσουσιν αὐτὸν καὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν, καὶ μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἀναστήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: And having taken again the twelve he began them to tell the things being about him to happen, \v 33 Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and to the scribes, and they will condemn him to death and will hand over him to the Gentiles, \v 34 and they will mock him and will spit upon him and will flog him and will kill, and after three days he will rise.

en.L: And taking the twelve aside again, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to tell them the things that were about to happen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: \v 33 "Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes, and they will condemn {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death and will hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to the Gentiles, \v 34 and they will mock {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and spit on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and flog {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and kill [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], and after three days {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rise."
en.B: Again {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the Twelve with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and began telling them the things that were about to happen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 33 "We are on our way up to Jerusalem," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "and there the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and scribes, who will condemn {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death and hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to the Gentiles. \v 34 They will make fun of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, spit on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, whip {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; and three days later {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rise."
en.R: Jesus took the Twelve away from the others again. He began to tell them the things that would soon happen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 33 He said, "Listen! We are going up to Jerusalem. There the Son of Man will be handed over to the leading priests and the teachers of God's law. They will decide that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} must die. Then they will hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to the Romans, who are not Jews. \v 34 They will laugh at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and spit on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They will beat {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with whips and kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But three days later {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will come back to life."

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại đem [nhóm] Mười Hai riêng ra, bắt đầu nói với họ những điều sắp xảy đến cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: \v 33 "Này, chúng ta đang đi lên Giê-ru-sa-lem, và Con Người sẽ bị nộp cho các thầy tế lễ cả và các thầy thông giáo; họ sẽ kết án tử hình {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và sẽ nộp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho dân ngoại; \v 34 họ sẽ chế nhạo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, khạc nhổ trên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, đánh đòn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và giết [{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}], và sau ba ngày {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ sống lại."
vi.B: Một lần nữa {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đem nhóm Mười Hai riêng ra và bắt đầu nói cho họ biết những việc sắp xảy đến cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \v 33 Ngài nói: "Chúng ta đang đi lên Giê-ru-sa-lem. Tại đó Con Người sẽ bị nộp cho các thầy tế lễ cả và các thầy thông giáo. Họ sẽ kết án tử hình {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và nộp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho dân ngoại. \v 34 Dân ngoại sẽ chế giễu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, khạc nhổ trên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, đánh đòn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và giết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; nhưng ba ngày sau {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ sống lại."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu lại đem mười hai môn đồ riêng ra. Ngài bắt đầu nói cho họ biết những việc sắp xảy đến cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \v 33 Ngài nói: "Hãy nghe đây! Chúng ta đang đi lên Giê-ru-sa-lem. Ở đó, Con Người sẽ bị nộp cho các thầy tế lễ cả và các thầy dạy luật. Họ sẽ quyết định rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phải chết. Rồi họ sẽ nộp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho người La Mã, là những người không phải Do Thái. \v 34 Người La Mã sẽ chế giễu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và khạc nhổ trên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ sẽ đánh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bằng roi và giết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Nhưng ba ngày sau {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ sống lại."

ko.L: 그리고 그분은 다시 열둘을 데리고 가셔서, 자기에게 일어날 일들을 그들에게 말씀하기 시작하셨다. \v 33 "보아라, 우리는 예루살렘으로 올라가고 있다. 그리고 인자는 대제사장들과 율법학자들에게 넘겨질 것이다. 그러면 그들은 그를 사형에 처하기로 판결하고 그를 이방인들에게 넘겨줄 것이다. \v 34 그리고 그들은 그를 조롱하고 그에게 침을 뱉고 그를 채찍질하고 [그를] 죽일 것이다. 그러나 사흘 후에 그는 살아날 것이다."
ko.B: 예수께서는 다시 열두 제자를 따로 데리고 가셔서, 앞으로 자기에게 일어날 일을 그들에게 말씀하기 시작하셨다. \v 33 "우리는 지금 예루살렘으로 올라가고 있다. 거기에서 인자는 대제사장들과 율법학자들에게 넘겨질 것이다. 그들은 그에게 사형 판결을 내리고 그를 이방인들에게 넘겨줄 것이다. \v 34 이방인들은 그를 조롱하고 그에게 침을 뱉고 채찍질하고 죽일 것이다. 그러나 그는 사흘 뒤에 다시 살아날 것이다."
ko.R: 예수께서는 다시 열두 제자만 따로 데리고 가셨다. 그리고 곧 자기에게 일어날 일들을 그들에게 말씀해 주기 시작하셨다. \v 33 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "잘 들어라! 우리는 지금 예루살렘으로 올라가고 있다. 거기에서 인자는 대제사장들과 율법을 가르치는 선생들에게 넘겨질 것이다. 그들은 그가 죽어야 한다고 판결할 것이다. 그리고 그를 유대인이 아닌 로마 사람들에게 넘겨줄 것이다. \v 34 그 사람들은 그를 비웃고, 그에게 침을 뱉고, 채찍으로 때리고, 죽일 것이다. 그러나 사흘 뒤에 그는 다시 살아날 것이다."

es.L: Y tomando aparte otra vez a los doce, comenzó a decirles las cosas que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} iban a suceder: \v 33 «{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, subimos a Jerusalén, y el Hijo del Hombre será entregado a los principales sacerdotes y a los escribas, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} condenarán a muerte y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} entregarán a los gentiles, \v 34 y se burlarán de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} escupirán, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} azotarán, y [{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}] matarán, y después de tres días resucitará».
es.B: Otra vez llamó aparte a los Doce y comenzó a decirles lo que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} iba a suceder. \v 33 «Ahora subimos a Jerusalén —les dijo—, y allí el Hijo del Hombre será entregado a los jefes de los sacerdotes y a los escribas. Ellos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} condenarán a muerte y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} entregarán a los gentiles. \v 34 Se burlarán de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} escupirán, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} azotarán y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} matarán; y tres días después resucitará».
es.R: Jesús volvió a llevar aparte a los Doce. Comenzó a decirles lo que pronto {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} iba a pasar. \v 33 Les dijo: «¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}! Vamos subiendo a Jerusalén. Allí el Hijo del Hombre será entregado a los jefes de los sacerdotes y a los maestros de la ley. Ellos decidirán que tiene que morir. Luego {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} entregarán a los romanos, que no son judíos. \v 34 Se reirán de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} escupirán. Lo golpearán con látigos y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} matarán. Pero tres días después volverá a la vida».

fr.L: Et prenant de nouveau les Douze avec [{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}], {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} commença à leur dire ce qui allait {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} arriver : \v 33 « Voici que nous montons à Jérusalem, et le Fils de l’homme sera livré aux chefs des prêtres et aux scribes, et ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} condamneront à mort et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} livreront aux nations, \v 34 et ils se moqueront de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et cracheront sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} flagelleront, et [{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}] tueront, et après trois jours {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ressuscitera. »
fr.B: De nouveau, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} prit les Douze avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et se mit à leur dire ce qui allait {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} arriver. \v 33 « Nous montons à Jérusalem, dit-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}, et là le Fils de l’homme sera livré aux chefs des prêtres et aux scribes. Ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} condamneront à mort et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} livreront aux non-Juifs. \v 34 Ils se moqueront de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, cracheront sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} fouetteront et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tueront ; et trois jours après, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ressuscitera. »
fr.R: Jésus a de nouveau pris les Douze à part. Il a commencé à leur dire ce qui allait bientôt {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} arriver. \v 33 Il a dit : « Écoutez ! Nous montons à Jérusalem. Là-bas, le Fils de l’homme sera livré aux chefs des prêtres et aux spécialistes de la Loi. Ils décideront qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} doit mourir. Puis ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} livreront aux Romains, qui ne sont pas juifs. \v 34 Ils se moqueront de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et cracheront sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} frapperont à coups de fouet et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tueront. Mais trois jours après, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} reviendra à la vie. »

sw.L: Na akiwachukua tena wale Kumi na Wawili, alianza kuwaambia mambo yaliyokuwa karibu kumpata: \v 33 "Tazama, tunapanda kwenda Yerusalemu, na Mwana wa Adamu atakabidhiwa kwa wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi, nao watamhukumu kifo na kumkabidhi kwa watu wa mataifa, \v 34 nao watamdhihaki, na kumtemea mate, na kumpiga mijeledi, na kumwua, na baada ya siku tatu atafufuka."
sw.B: Akawachukua tena wale Kumi na Wawili kando, akaanza kuwaeleza mambo yaliyokuwa karibu kumpata. \v 33 Akasema, "Sasa tunapanda kwenda Yerusalemu, na huko Mwana wa Adamu atakabidhiwa kwa wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi. Watamhukumu adhabu ya kifo na kumkabidhi kwa watu wa mataifa. \v 34 Watamfanyia mzaha, watamtemea mate, watampiga mijeledi na kumwua; na siku tatu baadaye atafufuka."
sw.R: Yesu aliwachukua tena wale Kumi na Wawili mbali na wengine. Akaanza kuwaambia mambo ambayo yangempata hivi karibuni. \v 33 Akasema, "Sikilizeni! Tunapanda kwenda Yerusalemu. Huko Mwana wa Adamu atakabidhiwa kwa viongozi wa makuhani na walimu wa sheria. Wataamua kwamba lazima afe. Kisha watamkabidhi kwa Warumi, ambao si Wayahudi. \v 34 Watamcheka na kumtemea mate. Watampiga kwa mijeledi na kumwua. Lakini siku tatu baadaye atafufuka."

pt.L: E, tomando outra vez os doze à parte, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} começou a lhes dizer as coisas que {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} iam acontecer: \v 33 "Vejam, estamos subindo para Jerusalém, e o Filho do Homem será entregue aos chefes dos sacerdotes e aos escribas, e eles {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} condenarão à morte e {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} entregarão às nações, \v 34 e zombarão {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, e cuspirão {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}, e {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} açoitarão, e [{{deity_pronoun:o|O}}] matarão, e depois de três dias {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} ressuscitará."
pt.B: Mais uma vez, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} levou os Doze à parte e começou a lhes contar o que estava para {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} acontecer. \v 33 "Estamos subindo para Jerusalém", disse {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}, "e lá o Filho do Homem será entregue aos chefes dos sacerdotes e aos escribas, que {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} condenarão à morte e {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} entregarão aos não judeus. \v 34 Eles vão zombar {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, cuspir {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}, açoitá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} e matá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}; e, três dias depois, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} ressuscitará."
pt.R: Jesus chamou os Doze de novo para longe dos outros. Ele começou a contar a eles as coisas que logo iam acontecer com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}. \v 33 Ele disse: "Escutem! Nós estamos subindo para Jerusalém. Lá o Filho do Homem vai ser entregue aos chefes dos sacerdotes e aos mestres da Lei. Eles vão decidir que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} deve morrer. Depois vão entregá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} aos romanos, que não são judeus. \v 34 Eles vão zombar {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}} e cuspir {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}. Vão bater {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}} com chicotes e matá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}. Mas três dias depois {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} vai voltar à vida."

decisions.choice: the third prediction of the passion: the fullest of the three
decisions.reason: Jesus has foretold his death and rising in 8:31 and 9:31. This time he names Jerusalem, the chief priests and scribes, the Gentiles, and the mocking, spitting and flogging. Each is told in 14:53-15:20.

decisions.choice: handed over: delivered up, first to the Jewish leaders, then by them to the Gentiles
decisions.reason: The same verb is used twice: the Son of Man is handed over to the chief priests and scribes, and they hand him over to the Gentiles (15:1).

decisions.choice: the Gentiles: the Roman governor and his soldiers
decisions.reason: The word means the nations, people who are not Jews. Here it means the Roman rulers, who alone could carry out a death sentence (15:1-20).

decisions.choice: after three days
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "on the third day", the wording of Matthew 20:19 and Luke 18:33. The SBLGNT reads "after three days", as Mark has it in 8:31 and 9:31. Both mean the same. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: taking aside: taking with him apart from the others
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the Twelve alone, away from those who were following.

decisions.choice: kill: the Greek leaves "him" to be understood
decisions.reason: The object is clear from the verbs before it.

decisions.choice: handed over
decisions.reason: All levels say "handed over", as in 9:31, since the verb is wider than betrayal and is used for both steps here.

decisions.choice: the Romans, who are not Jews; come back to life
decisions.reason: Readable says who the Gentiles were in this case and what rising means.

decisions.choice: "các thầy tế lễ cả" (L, B, R); "các thầy thông giáo" (L, B), "các thầy dạy luật" (R)
decisions.reason: As John 11:47 and Mark 9:11: the Protestant terms the style guide settles, with a plain description of the scribes at Readable.

decisions.choice: "bị nộp", "nộp" for "handed over", at every level
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 9:31, so the predictions read as one thread.

decisions.choice: "dân ngoại" for the Gentiles (L, B)
decisions.reason: The usual word for the non-Jewish nations; Readable names the Romans, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "넘겨지다", "넘겨주다" at every level; "인자" (Readable explained it at 9:9)
decisions.reason: As at 9:31: one verb for handing over, first to the Jewish leaders, then by them to the Gentiles (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "이방인들" (L, B); "유대인이 아닌 로마 사람들" (R)
decisions.reason: The Gentiles here are the Roman governor and his soldiers (meaning decision); Readable names them, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: [그를]
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves "him" to be understood with "kill" (meaning decision); Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: principales sacerdotes (L); jefes de los sacerdotes (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in John's Spanish: Literal keeps the traditional title; Balanced and Readable say plainly that they were the heads of the priesthood.

decisions.choice: escribas (L, B); maestros de la ley (R)
decisions.reason: As in 9:11: Readable says what the scribes were.

decisions.choice: entregado, entregarán
decisions.reason: The same verb twice, as in English "handed over": first to the Jewish leaders, then by them to the Gentiles.

decisions.choice: les chefs des prêtres (L, B, R); les scribes (L, B); les spécialistes de la Loi (R)
decisions.reason: As the French John (8:3; 11:47) and Mark 9. "Les chefs des prêtres" names the leading priests as a group, where "les grands prêtres" suggests several holders of the one office of high priest.

decisions.choice: les nations (L); les non-Juifs (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek word means "the nations", the peoples other than Israel (meaning decision: here the Roman governor and his soldiers). Literal keeps "les nations" as the French letters do; Balanced says "les non-Juifs", as the French Ephesians does, since "païens" now suggests irreligion; Readable names the Romans, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: wakuu wa makuhani (L, B), viongozi wa makuhani (R); waandishi (L, B), walimu wa sheria (R)
decisions.reason: "Wakuu wa makuhani" is the term Swahili John uses for the chief priests, with Readable saying what they were, "viongozi wa makuhani", as in 14:1 and 15:1. The scribes are "waandishi" with "walimu wa sheria" at Readable, as in chapter 9.

decisions.choice: kumwua, with no bracket
decisions.reason: The English Literal brackets "[him]" after "kill" because the Greek leaves it out. Swahili marks the object inside the verb (kumwua), so nothing is supplied.

source.text: Καὶ προσπορεύονται αὐτῷ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωάννης οἱ υἱοὶ Ζεβεδαίου λέγοντες αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, θέλομεν ἵνα ὃ ἐὰν αἰτήσωμέν σε ποιήσῃς ἡμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: And come up to him James and John the sons of Zebedee saying to him, Teacher, we desire that whatever we might ask you you would do for us.

en.L: And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, come up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, we want {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to do for us whatever we ask {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.B: Then James and John, Zebedee's sons, came up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. "Teacher," they said, "we would like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to do whatever we ask of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.R: Then James and John, the two sons of Zebedee, came to Jesus. They said, "Teacher, please do for us whatever we ask."

vi.L: Và Gia-cơ và Giăng, hai con trai của Xê-bê-đê, đến gần {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa Thầy, chúng con muốn Thầy làm cho chúng con bất cứ điều gì chúng con xin Thầy."
vi.B: Bấy giờ Gia-cơ và Giăng, hai con trai của Xê-bê-đê, đến gần {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và nói: "Thưa Thầy, chúng con mong Thầy làm cho chúng con bất cứ điều gì chúng con xin."
vi.R: Rồi Gia-cơ và Giăng, hai con trai của ông Xê-bê-đê, đến gặp Đức Giê-xu. Họ nói: "Thưa Thầy, xin Thầy làm cho chúng con bất cứ điều gì chúng con xin."

ko.L: 그리고 세베대의 아들들인 야고보와 요한이 그분께 다가와서 그분께 말한다. "선생님, 저희가 무엇을 구하든지 저희에게 해 주시기를 바랍니다."
ko.B: 그때 세베대의 아들 야고보와 요한이 예수께 다가와서 말했다. "선생님, 저희가 무엇을 구하든지 들어주시기를 바랍니다."
ko.R: 그때 세베대의 두 아들 야고보와 요한이 예수께 와서 말했다. "선생님, 저희가 부탁드리는 것을 무엇이든 들어주십시오."

es.L: Y se {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} acercan Santiago y Juan, los hijos de Zebedeo, diciéndole: «Maestro, queremos que hagas por nosotros lo que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} pidamos».
es.B: Entonces Santiago y Juan, los hijos de Zebedeo, se {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} acercaron. «Maestro —{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron—, queremos que nos concedas lo que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} vamos a pedir».
es.R: Entonces Santiago y Juan, los dos hijos de Zebedeo, se acercaron a Jesús. Le dijeron: «Maestro, por favor, haz por nosotros lo que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} pidamos».

fr.L: Et Jacques et Jean, les fils de Zébédée, s’approchent de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} disant : « Maître, nous voulons que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fasses pour nous ce que nous {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} demanderons. »
fr.B: Alors Jacques et Jean, les fils de Zébédée, s’approchèrent de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. « Maître, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dirent-ils, nous voudrions que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fasses pour nous tout ce que nous allons {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} demander. »
fr.R: Puis Jacques et Jean, les deux fils de Zébédée, sont venus voir Jésus. Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont dit : « Maître, nous voudrions que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fasses pour nous tout ce que nous allons demander. »

sw.L: Na Yakobo na Yohana, wana wa Zebedayo, wanamjia, wakimwambia, "Mwalimu, tunataka utufanyie lolote tutakalokuomba."
sw.B: Kisha Yakobo na Yohana, wana wa Zebedayo, wakamjia, wakasema, "Mwalimu, tungependa utufanyie chochote tutakachokuomba."
sw.R: Kisha Yakobo na Yohana, wana wawili wa Zebedayo, wakaja kwa Yesu. Wakasema, "Mwalimu, tafadhali utufanyie lolote tutakalokuomba."

pt.L: E Tiago e João, os filhos de Zebedeu, vêm até {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}, dizendo-{{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}}: "Mestre, queremos que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} faças por nós o que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} pedirmos."
pt.B: Então Tiago e João, os filhos de Zebedeu, aproximaram-se {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}. "Mestre", disseram eles, "gostaríamos que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fizesses por nós qualquer coisa que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} pedíssemos."
pt.R: Então Tiago e João, os dois filhos de Zebedeu, foram até Jesus. Eles disseram: "Mestre, por favor, faz por nós o que vamos pedir."

decisions.choice: come up: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: whatever we ask: an open request for a favor
decisions.reason: Right after Jesus has spoken of his death (10:33-34), the two ask for honor for themselves. The request is like Herod's open promise in 6:22-23.

decisions.choice: James and John: two of the first four called (1:19-20)
alternatives: other men named James and John
decisions.reason: With Peter they saw the raising of Jairus's daughter (5:37) and the transfiguration (9:2). Jesus named them Boanerges, sons of thunder (3:17).

decisions.choice: please do for us whatever we ask
alternatives: we want you to do for us whatever we ask you
decisions.reason: Readable puts the request in a simple form.

decisions.choice: "Gia-cơ", "Giăng", "Xê-bê-đê"
decisions.reason: The Protestant forms of the names, settled for the whole Bible.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί θέλετε ποιήσω ὑμῖν;

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, What do you desire I should do for you?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "What do you want {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?"
en.B: "What would you like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them.
en.R: Jesus asked them, "What would you like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?"

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Các con muốn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm gì cho các con?"
vi.B: Ngài hỏi họ: "Các con muốn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm gì cho các con?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu hỏi họ: "Các con muốn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm gì cho các con?"

fr.B: « Que voulez-vous que je fasse pour vous ? » leur demanda-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}.
fr.R: Jésus leur a demandé : « Qu’est-ce que vous voulez que je fasse pour vous ? »

pt.B: "O que vocês gostariam que eu fizesse por vocês?", {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes perguntou.

decisions.reason: Mark sets the two answers side by side. The brothers ask for glory; the blind man asks to see.

decisions.choice: want ... I should do: Jesus does not promise until he hears the request
alternatives: he agrees to do whatever they ask
decisions.reason: He asks them to say what they want before he answers.

source.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Δὸς ἡμῖν ἵνα εἷς σου ἐκ δεξιῶν καὶ εἷς ἐξ ἀριστερῶν καθίσωμεν ἐν τῇ δόξῃ σου.

records.literal_gloss: And they said to him, Grant to us that one of you at right and one at left we might sit in the glory of you.

en.L: And they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Grant us that we may sit, one at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right and one at [{{deity_pronoun:your|Your}}] left, in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory."
en.B: They answered, "Grant that when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory, one of us may sit on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right and one on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} left."
en.R: They answered, "When {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rule as King in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory, let one of us sit at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right side and the other at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} left side."

vi.L: Và họ thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Xin cho chúng con được ngồi, một người bên phải Thầy và một người bên trái [Thầy], trong vinh quang của Thầy."
vi.B: Họ thưa: "Khi Thầy ở trong vinh quang của Thầy, xin cho một người trong chúng con được ngồi bên phải Thầy, và một người bên trái Thầy."
vi.R: Họ thưa: "Khi Thầy cai trị làm Vua trong vinh quang, xin cho một người trong chúng con được ngồi bên phải Thầy, và người kia ngồi bên trái Thầy."

ko.L: 그러자 그들이 그분께 말했다. "선생님의 영광 가운데서, 저희 가운데 하나는 선생님의 오른쪽에, 하나는 [선생님의] 왼쪽에 앉게 해 주십시오."
ko.B: 그들이 말했다. "선생님께서 영광을 받으실 때에, 저희 가운데 하나는 선생님의 오른쪽에, 하나는 왼쪽에 앉게 해 주십시오."
ko.R: 그들이 대답했다. "선생님께서 영광스러운 왕이 되셔서 다스리실 때, 저희 가운데 한 사람은 선생님의 오른쪽에, 또 한 사람은 왼쪽에 앉게 해 주십시오."

es.L: Y ellos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «Concédenos que nos sentemos, uno a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} derecha y uno a [{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}] izquierda, en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} gloria».
es.B: Ellos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondieron: «Concédenos que, cuando estés en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} gloria, uno de nosotros se siente a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} derecha y el otro a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} izquierda».
es.R: Ellos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondieron: «Cuando reines como Rey en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} gloria, deja que uno de nosotros se siente a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} lado derecho y el otro a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} lado izquierdo».

fr.L: Et ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dirent : « Accorde-nous de siéger, l’un à {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} droite et l’autre à [{{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}] gauche, dans {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} gloire. »
fr.B: Ils répondirent : « Accorde-nous, quand {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} seras dans {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} gloire, de siéger l’un à {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} droite et l’autre à {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} gauche. »
fr.R: Ils ont répondu : « Quand {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} régneras comme roi dans {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} gloire, laisse l’un de nous s’asseoir à {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} droite et l’autre à {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} gauche. »

sw.L: Nao wakamwambia, "Utujalie tuketi, mmoja upande {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wa kulia na mmoja upande wa kushoto, katika utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}."
sw.B: Wakamjibu, "Utakapokuwa katika utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, utujalie mmoja wetu aketi upande {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wa kulia na mwingine upande {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wa kushoto."
sw.R: Wakajibu, "Utakapotawala kama Mfalme katika utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, mmoja wetu aketi upande {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wa kulia, na mwingine upande {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wa kushoto."

pt.L: E eles {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} disseram: "Concede-nos que nos sentemos, um à {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} direita e um à [{{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}}] esquerda, na {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} glória."
pt.B: Eles responderam: "Permite que, quando {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} estiveres na {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} glória, um de nós se sente à {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} direita e o outro à {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} esquerda."
pt.R: Eles responderam: "Quando {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} reinares como Rei na {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} glória, deixa um de nós sentar do {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} lado direito e o outro do {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} lado esquerdo."

decisions.choice: at your right and at your left: the places of highest honor beside a king
decisions.reason: The seat at a king's right hand was the place of greatest honor and power (1 Kings 2:19; Psalm 110:1), and the left the next.

decisions.choice: your glory: the glory of the Son of Man when he comes as king
decisions.reason: Jesus has spoken of the Son of Man coming in the glory of his Father (8:38). The brothers expect him to rule soon.

decisions.choice: the request misunderstands Jesus' path
decisions.reason: They believe Jesus will reign, but they have not grasped that his way to glory is through death (10:33-34). At the cross the places at his right and left are taken by two rebels (15:27).

decisions.choice: When you rule as King in your glory
decisions.reason: Readable says what the brothers expect Jesus' glory to be.

decisions.choice: "영광" at every level
decisions.reason: Key term, as in the Korean John (style guide, section 6). Readable adds that he will reign as king, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: [선생님의]
decisions.reason: The Greek gives "your" only with "right"; Korean repeats it before "left", and Literal brackets it.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ οἴδατε τί αἰτεῖσθε· δύνασθε πιεῖν τὸ ποτήριον ὃ ἐγὼ πίνω, ἢ τὸ βάπτισμα ὃ ἐγὼ βαπτίζομαι βαπτισθῆναι;

records.literal_gloss: And Jesus said to them, Not you know what you ask. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, or the baptism that I am baptized to be baptized?

en.L: But Jesus said to them, "You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, or to be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?"
en.B: Jesus said to them, "You have no idea what you are asking for. Can you drink the cup that I am drinking, or be baptized with the baptism I am going through?"
en.R: Jesus said to them, "You do not understand what you are asking. I must drink a cup of suffering. Can you drink it? I must go through a baptism of suffering. Can you go through it?"

vi.L: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Các con không biết điều mình đang xin. Các con có thể uống chén mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} uống, hoặc chịu báp-têm mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chịu không?"
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu bảo họ: "Các con không biết mình đang xin gì. Các con có thể uống chén {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang uống, hay chịu báp-têm mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang chịu không?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Các con không hiểu điều mình đang xin. Ta phải uống một chén đau khổ. Các con có thể uống chén ấy không? Ta phải chịu một báp-têm đau khổ. Các con có thể chịu báp-têm ấy không?"

ko.L: 그러나 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "너희는 너희가 구하는 것이 무엇인지 알지 못한다. 내가 마시는 잔을 너희가 마실 수 있느냐? 또는 내가 받는 세례를 너희가 받을 수 있느냐?"
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "너희는 너희가 무엇을 구하는지 모르고 있다. 내가 마시는 잔을 너희가 마실 수 있느냐? 내가 받는 세례를 너희가 받을 수 있느냐?"
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "너희는 무엇을 구하는지 모르고 있다. 나는 고난의 잔을 마셔야 한다. 너희도 그 잔을 마실 수 있느냐? 나는 고난의 세례를 받아야 한다. 너희도 그 세례를 받을 수 있느냐?"

es.L: Pero Jesús les dijo: «No {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} lo que {{plural_you:piden|pedís}}. ¿{{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}} beber la copa que yo bebo, o ser bautizados con el bautismo con que yo soy bautizado?».
es.B: Jesús les dijo: «No {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} idea de lo que {{plural_you:piden|pedís}}. ¿{{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}} beber la copa que yo bebo, o ser bautizados con el bautismo que yo recibo?».
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «No {{plural_you:entienden|entendéis}} lo que {{plural_you:piden|pedís}}. Yo tengo que beber una copa de sufrimiento. ¿{{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}} beberla? Tengo que pasar por un bautismo de sufrimiento. ¿{{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}} pasar por él?».

fr.L: Mais Jésus leur dit : « Vous ne savez pas ce que vous demandez. Pouvez-vous boire la coupe que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je bois, ou être baptisés du baptême dont {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je suis baptisé ? »
fr.B: Jésus leur dit : « Vous ne savez pas ce que vous demandez. Pouvez-vous boire la coupe que je bois, ou être baptisés du baptême par lequel je passe ? »
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Vous ne comprenez pas ce que vous demandez. Je dois boire une coupe de souffrance. Pouvez-vous la boire ? Je dois passer par un baptême de souffrance. Pouvez-vous y passer ? »

sw.L: Lakini Yesu akawaambia, "Hamjui mnaloliomba. Mnaweza kunywa kikombe ninachokinywa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, au kubatizwa ubatizo ambao {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninabatizwa?"
sw.B: Yesu akawaambia, "Hamjui mnachoomba. Je, mnaweza kunywa kikombe ninachokinywa, au kubatizwa kwa ubatizo ninaoupitia?"
sw.R: Yesu akawaambia, "Hamwelewi mnachoomba. Ni lazima ninywe kikombe cha mateso. Je, mnaweza kukinywa? Ni lazima nipitie ubatizo wa mateso. Je, mnaweza kuupitia?"

pt.L: Mas Jesus lhes disse: "Vocês não sabem o que estão pedindo. Podem beber o cálice que eu bebo, ou ser batizados com o batismo com que eu sou batizado?"
pt.B: Jesus lhes disse: "Vocês não fazem ideia do que estão pedindo. Vocês podem beber o cálice que eu estou bebendo, ou ser batizados com o batismo pelo qual eu estou passando?"
pt.R: Jesus disse a eles: "Vocês não entendem o que estão pedindo. Eu preciso beber um cálice de sofrimento. Vocês conseguem beber esse cálice? Eu preciso passar por um batismo de sofrimento. Vocês conseguem passar por ele?"

decisions.choice: the cup: the suffering God gives him to bear
alternatives: a cup of wine at a feast
decisions.reason: In the prophets the cup stands for God's judgment, which the wicked must drink (Isaiah 51:17; Jeremiah 25:15; Psalm 75:9). In Gethsemane Jesus prays that this cup may be taken from him (14:36).

decisions.choice: the baptism: being overwhelmed by suffering, as by deep water
alternatives: the rite of baptism in water
decisions.reason: The verb means to be plunged under. The Psalms speak of trouble as floods that cover a person (Psalm 69:2-3; 42:8). Luke 12:50 has a similar saying about Jesus' death.

decisions.choice: drink, am baptized: present tenses, the suffering already begun or certain
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of his suffering as already under way.

decisions.choice: a cup of suffering; a baptism of suffering
decisions.reason: Readable says what the cup and the baptism stand for, which the other levels leave as pictures.

decisions.choice: "chén" for the cup and "báp-têm" for the baptism
decisions.reason: "báp-têm" is the settled Protestant word; both pictures are kept, and Readable names them "chén đau khổ", "báp-têm đau khổ", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "내가 받는 세례를 받다" for the baptism with which I am baptized
decisions.reason: Korean says one receives a baptism ("세례를 받다"); the Greek's repeated "baptized with the baptism" becomes one verb and its object at every level without losing a word of meaning. Readable names the suffering, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: copa; bautismo
decisions.reason: Both pictures are kept at every level (meaning decisions); "copa" rather than "vaso", since it is the cup God gives to drink.

decisions.choice: que moi, je bois; dont moi, je suis baptisé (L)
alternatives: que je bois; dont je suis baptisé
decisions.reason: The Greek adds the pronoun "I" to both verbs; French Literal shows the stress with "moi, je". Also in 10:39.

decisions.choice: mimi for the emphatic "I"
decisions.reason: The Greek adds an emphatic "I" in both clauses. Swahili shows it with the free pronoun "mimi", which takes the deity_pronoun span because Jesus speaks of himself; the English has no span on "I".

source.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Δυνάμεθα.

vi.R: Họ đáp: "Thưa được, chúng con làm được."
