decisions.choice: we are able: a confident answer that they do not yet understand
alternatives: they know exactly what he means
decisions.reason: When Jesus is arrested, all the disciples run away (14:50).

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τὸ ποτήριον ὃ ἐγὼ πίνω πίεσθε καὶ τὸ βάπτισμα ὃ ἐγὼ βαπτίζομαι βαπτισθήσεσθε, τὸ δὲ καθίσαι ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἢ ἐξ εὐωνύμων οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὸν δοῦναι, ἀλλ’ οἷς ἡτοίμασται.

records.literal_gloss: And Jesus said to them, The cup that I drink you will drink, and the baptism that I am baptized you will be baptized; \v 40 but to sit at right of me or at left not is mine to give, but for whom it has been prepared.

en.L: And Jesus said to them, "The cup that I drink you will drink, and with the baptism with which I am baptized you will be baptized; \v 40 but to sit at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right or at [{{deity_pronoun:my|My}}] left is not {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} to give, but [it is] for those for whom it has been prepared."
en.B: Jesus told them, "The cup I drink, you will drink, and with the baptism I am going through you too will be baptized. \v 40 But a seat at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right or at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} left is not mine to grant. Those places belong to the ones for whom they have been prepared."
en.R: Then Jesus said to them, "You will drink from the same cup of suffering as I do. You will go through the same baptism of suffering. \v 40 But I am not the one who chooses who will sit at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right side or at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} left side. God has prepared those places for the people he has chosen."

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Chén {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} uống, các con sẽ uống; và báp-têm {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chịu, các con sẽ chịu; \v 40 nhưng việc ngồi bên phải {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} hay bên trái [{{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}] thì không phải [quyền] của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ban cho, nhưng [là] cho những người mà [chỗ ấy] đã được dọn sẵn."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu bảo họ: "Chén {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} uống, các con cũng sẽ uống; báp-têm {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chịu, các con cũng sẽ chịu. \v 40 Nhưng ngồi bên phải hay bên trái {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì không phải {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là người ban cho. Những chỗ ấy đã được dọn sẵn cho ai thì thuộc về người ấy."
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Các con sẽ uống cùng một chén đau khổ như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Các con sẽ chịu cùng một báp-têm đau khổ như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \v 40 Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không phải là người chọn ai sẽ ngồi bên phải hay bên trái {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Đức Chúa Trời đã dọn sẵn những chỗ ấy cho những người {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã chọn."

ko.L: 그러자 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "내가 마시는 잔을 너희가 마실 것이고, 내가 받는 세례를 너희가 받을 것이다. \v 40 그러나 내 오른쪽이나 왼쪽에 앉는 것은 내가 줄 수 있는 것이 아니라, 그 자리가 준비된 사람들의 것이다."
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "너희는 내가 마시는 잔을 마실 것이고, 내가 받는 세례를 받을 것이다. \v 40 그러나 내 오른쪽이나 왼쪽에 앉는 것은 내가 정해 줄 수 있는 것이 아니다. 그 자리는 그것이 마련된 사람들의 것이다."
ko.R: 그러자 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "너희는 내가 마시는 것과 같은 고난의 잔을 마실 것이다. 내가 받는 것과 같은 고난의 세례도 받을 것이다. \v 40 그러나 내 오른쪽이나 왼쪽에 누가 앉을지는 내가 정하는 것이 아니다. 하나님께서 그 자리를 마련해 두신 사람들이 따로 있다."

es.L: Y Jesús les dijo: «La copa que yo bebo, la {{plural_you:beberán|beberéis}}, y con el bautismo con que yo soy bautizado {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} bautizados; \v 40 pero el sentarse a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} derecha o a [{{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}}] izquierda no es {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}} darlo, sino [que es] para quienes ha sido preparado».
es.B: Jesús les dijo: «La copa que yo bebo, la {{plural_you:beberán|beberéis}}, y {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} bautizados con el bautismo que yo recibo. \v 40 Pero sentarse a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} derecha o a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} izquierda no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} corresponde a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} concederlo. Esos lugares son de aquellos para quienes han sido preparados».
es.R: Entonces Jesús les dijo: «{{plural_you:Beberán|Beberéis}} de la misma copa de sufrimiento que yo. {{plural_you:Pasarán|Pasaréis}} por el mismo bautismo de sufrimiento. \v 40 Pero no soy yo quien decide quién se sentará a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} lado derecho o a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} lado izquierdo. Dios ha preparado esos lugares para las personas que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha escogido».

fr.L: Et Jésus leur dit : « La coupe que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je bois, vous la boirez, et du baptême dont {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je suis baptisé, vous serez baptisés ; \v 40 mais siéger à {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} droite ou à [{{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}}] gauche, il ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}appartient pas de l’accorder, mais [c’est] pour ceux à qui cela a été préparé. »
fr.B: Jésus leur dit : « La coupe que je bois, vous la boirez, et du baptême par lequel je passe, vous serez baptisés vous aussi. \v 40 Mais siéger à {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} droite ou à {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} gauche, ce n’est pas à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} de l’accorder. Ces places reviennent à ceux pour qui elles ont été préparées. »
fr.R: Alors Jésus leur a dit : « Vous boirez la même coupe de souffrance que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Vous passerez par le même baptême de souffrance. \v 40 Mais ce n’est pas {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui choisis qui sera assis à {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} droite ou à {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} gauche. Dieu a préparé ces places pour ceux qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a choisis. »

sw.L: Naye Yesu akawaambia, "Kikombe ninachokinywa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} mtakinywa, na ubatizo ambao {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninabatizwa mtabatizwa; \v 40 lakini kuketi upande {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wa kulia au wa kushoto si {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} kutoa, bali [ni kwa] wale ambao imeandaliwa kwa ajili yao."
sw.B: Yesu akawaambia, "Kikombe ninachokinywa mtakinywa, na ubatizo ninaoupitia mtabatizwa nao. \v 40 Lakini kuketi upande {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wa kulia au wa kushoto si {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} kutoa. Nafasi hizo ni za wale ambao zimeandaliwa kwa ajili yao."
sw.R: Kisha Yesu akawaambia, "Mtakunywa kikombe kile kile cha mateso ninachokinywa. Mtapitia ubatizo ule ule wa mateso ninaoupitia. \v 40 Lakini si {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninayechagua nani ataketi upande {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wa kulia au upande {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wa kushoto. Mungu ameziandaa nafasi hizo kwa ajili ya wale aliowachagua."

pt.L: E Jesus lhes disse: "O cálice que eu bebo vocês beberão, e com o batismo com que eu sou batizado vocês serão batizados; \v 40 mas sentar-se à {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} direita ou à [{{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}}] esquerda não cabe a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} conceder, mas [é] para aqueles para quem foi preparado."
pt.B: Jesus lhes disse: "O cálice que eu bebo vocês vão beber, e com o batismo pelo qual eu passo vocês também serão batizados. \v 40 Mas um lugar à {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} direita ou à {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} esquerda não cabe a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} conceder. Esses lugares pertencem àqueles para quem foram preparados."
pt.R: Então Jesus disse a eles: "Vocês vão beber do mesmo cálice de sofrimento que eu. Vocês vão passar pelo mesmo batismo de sofrimento. \v 40 Mas não sou eu quem escolhe quem vai se sentar do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} lado direito ou do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} lado esquerdo. Deus preparou esses lugares para as pessoas que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} escolheu."

decisions.choice: you will drink, you will be baptized: they will share his suffering
decisions.reason: Jesus promises them suffering, not seats of honor. Acts 12:2 tells that Herod Agrippa put James to death with the sword.

decisions.choice: has been prepared: a passive, God is the one who prepared it
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the actor unnamed, a common way of speaking of God's action. Matthew 20:23 says "by my Father".

decisions.choice: at my right or left: perhaps pointing ahead to the cross
decisions.reason: In 15:27 two rebels are crucified with Jesus, one on his right and one on his left. Mark may want readers to see the irony.

decisions.choice: God has prepared those places for the people he has chosen
alternatives: for whom it has been prepared
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who prepares, as the passive implies.

decisions.choice: "không phải [quyền] của Ta ban cho"
alternatives: "không phải của Ta để ban cho"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese needs a noun for "mine" in "not mine to give".

decisions.choice: "하나님께서 ... 마련해 두신"
decisions.reason: The passive means God prepared it (meaning decision); Readable names him, as the English Readable does. Literal and Balanced keep the passive "준비된", "마련된".

decisions.choice: si langu kutoa (not mine to give)
decisions.reason: "Langu" agrees with an understood "jambo" (matter): it is not my matter to give. As a free possessive for Jesus it takes the deity_pronoun span, as "mine" does in the English Literal.

source.text: Καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ δέκα ἤρξαντο ἀγανακτεῖν περὶ Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰωάννου.

records.literal_gloss: And having heard the ten began to be indignant about James and John.

en.L: And when the ten heard [it], they began to be indignant about James and John.
en.B: When the other ten heard about this, they became angry with James and John.
en.R: The other ten followers heard about this. They were angry with James and John.

vi.L: Và khi mười [người kia] nghe [điều đó], họ bắt đầu bất bình về Gia-cơ và Giăng.
vi.B: Khi mười môn đồ kia nghe chuyện này, họ bắt đầu bực tức với Gia-cơ và Giăng.
vi.R: Mười môn đồ kia nghe biết chuyện này. Họ giận Gia-cơ và Giăng.

ko.L: 그리고 열 [제자가] 듣고, 야고보와 요한에게 분개하기 시작했다.
ko.B: 다른 열 제자가 이 말을 듣고 야고보와 요한에게 화를 냈다.
ko.R: 다른 열 제자가 이 일을 알게 되었다. 그들은 야고보와 요한에게 화가 났다.

es.L: Y al oír [esto] los diez, comenzaron a indignarse contra Santiago y Juan.
es.B: Cuando los otros diez se enteraron, se indignaron con Santiago y Juan.
es.R: Los otros diez discípulos se enteraron de esto. Se molestaron mucho con Santiago y Juan.

fr.L: Et ayant entendu [cela], les dix commencèrent à s’indigner contre Jacques et Jean.
fr.B: Quand les dix autres apprirent cela, ils se mirent en colère contre Jacques et Jean.
fr.R: Les dix autres disciples ont appris ce qui s’était passé. Ils étaient fâchés contre Jacques et Jean.

sw.L: Na wale kumi waliposikia [hayo], walianza kuwakasirikia Yakobo na Yohana.
sw.B: Wale kumi wengine waliposikia habari hiyo, wakawakasirikia Yakobo na Yohana.
sw.R: Wale wanafunzi kumi wengine walisikia jambo hilo. Wakawakasirikia Yakobo na Yohana.

pt.L: E, ouvindo [isso], os dez começaram a se indignar contra Tiago e João.
pt.B: Quando os outros dez souberam disso, ficaram indignados com Tiago e João.
pt.R: Os outros dez seguidores ficaram sabendo disso. Eles ficaram com raiva de Tiago e João.

decisions.choice: be indignant: angry at what they felt was wrong
decisions.reason: The same word is used of Jesus in 10:14.

decisions.choice: the ten were angry: they wanted the same honor
decisions.reason: Their anger shows they too were thinking of rank, as in 9:34. Jesus speaks to all twelve in 10:42-45.

decisions.choice: the other ten
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the ten are the rest of the Twelve.

decisions.choice: [제자가]
decisions.reason: Korean does not use a bare number as a noun for people here; Literal brackets the noun.

source.text: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ δοκοῦντες ἄρχειν τῶν ἐθνῶν κατακυριεύουσιν αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ μεγάλοι αὐτῶν κατεξουσιάζουσιν αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And having called near them Jesus says to them, You know that those being accounted to rule the Gentiles exercise lordship over them, and the great ones of them exercise authority over them.

en.L: And calling them to [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], Jesus says to them, "You know that those who are considered rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
en.B: Jesus called them to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and told them, "You know that those who are thought of as rulers of the nations lord it over their people, and their important men use their power over them.
en.R: Jesus called them all together and said, "You know how it is with the people who rule over the nations. They like to show that they are the masters. Their leaders use their power to control people.

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu gọi họ lại [với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}] và nói với họ: "Các con biết rằng những người được xem là cai trị dân ngoại thì thống trị họ, và những người quyền thế của họ thì dùng quyền lực trên họ.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu gọi họ lại và bảo: "Các con biết rằng những người được coi là cai trị các dân tộc thì thống trị dân mình, và những kẻ quyền thế thì dùng quyền lực đè nén dân.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu gọi tất cả các môn đồ lại và nói: "Các con biết những người cai trị các dân tộc là thế nào rồi. Họ thích tỏ ra mình là chủ. Những người lãnh đạo của họ dùng quyền lực để kiểm soát dân chúng.

ko.L: 그러자 예수께서 그들을 불러 놓고 그들에게 말씀하신다. "너희가 알다시피, 이방인들의 통치자로 여겨지는 사람들은 그들 위에 군림하고, 그들의 큰 사람들은 그들 위에 권세를 부린다.
ko.B: 예수께서 그들을 가까이 불러 놓고 말씀하셨다. "너희도 알다시피, 민족들을 다스린다는 사람들은 백성 위에 군림하고, 높은 사람들은 백성에게 권력을 휘두른다.
ko.R: 예수께서 제자들을 모두 불러 모으시고 말씀하셨다. "세상 나라들을 다스리는 사람들이 어떤지 너희도 알고 있다. 그들은 자기가 주인이라는 것을 보여 주고 싶어 한다. 높은 사람들은 자기 힘으로 백성을 마음대로 부린다.

es.L: Y Jesús, llamándolos, les dice: «{{plural_you:Saben|Sabéis}} que los que son tenidos por gobernantes de los gentiles se enseñorean de ellos, y sus grandes ejercen autoridad sobre ellos.
es.B: Jesús los llamó y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Saben|Sabéis}} que los que son considerados gobernantes de las naciones las dominan como señores, y que sus grandes imponen su autoridad sobre ellas.
es.R: Jesús los llamó a todos y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Ya saben|Ya sabéis}} cómo son los que gobiernan las naciones. Les gusta mostrar que son los amos. Sus jefes usan su poder para controlar a la gente.

fr.L: Et les ayant appelés auprès [de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}], Jésus leur dit : « Vous savez que ceux qui sont considérés comme gouvernant les nations les dominent en seigneurs, et que leurs grands exercent sur elles leur pouvoir.
fr.B: Jésus les appela auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et leur dit : « Vous savez que ceux qu’on regarde comme les chefs des nations les dominent en maîtres, et que leurs grands personnages font peser sur elles leur pouvoir.
fr.R: Jésus les a tous appelés et leur a dit : « Vous savez comment font ceux qui gouvernent les peuples. Ils aiment montrer qu’ils sont les maîtres. Leurs chefs se servent de leur pouvoir pour commander les gens.

sw.L: Na Yesu, akiwaita [{{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}], anawaambia, "Mnajua kwamba wale wanaodhaniwa kuwa watawala wa watu wa mataifa huwatawala kwa mabavu, na wakuu wao huwatumia mamlaka juu yao.
sw.B: Yesu akawaita {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, akawaambia, "Mnajua kwamba wale wanaohesabiwa kuwa watawala wa mataifa huwatawala watu wao kwa mabavu, na wakubwa wao huwaonyesha mamlaka yao.
sw.R: Yesu akawaita wote pamoja, akasema, "Mnajua jinsi ilivyo kwa watu wanaotawala mataifa. Wanapenda kuonyesha kwamba wao ndio mabwana. Viongozi wao hutumia mamlaka yao kuwatawala watu.

pt.L: E Jesus, chamando-os para junto [de {{deity_pronoun:si|Si}}], lhes diz: "Vocês sabem que os que são considerados governantes das nações as dominam como senhores, e os seus grandes exercem autoridade sobre elas.
pt.B: Jesus os chamou para perto de {{deity_pronoun:si|Si}} e lhes disse: "Vocês sabem que aqueles que são tidos como governantes das nações dominam o seu povo como donos, e os seus homens importantes usam o poder sobre ele.
pt.R: Jesus chamou todos eles e disse: "Vocês sabem como é com as pessoas que governam as nações. Elas gostam de mostrar que são os donos. Os seus líderes usam o poder para controlar as pessoas.

decisions.choice: considered: those who are thought to rule, or recognized as rulers
alternatives: those who only pretend to rule
decisions.reason: The word can simply mean recognized. It may also hint that their rule is only apparent, since God is the true ruler.

decisions.choice: lord it over, exercise authority over: rule harshly, using power for themselves
decisions.reason: Both verbs are strengthened forms that suggest power used against those under it.

decisions.choice: the Gentiles: the nations of the world and their rulers
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of the way kings and governors of the nations rule, as Rome ruled at that time.

decisions.choice: says: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: They like to show that they are the masters
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom.

decisions.choice: "dân ngoại" (L); "các dân tộc" (B, R) for the nations
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal keeps the word used in 10:33, Balanced and Readable speak of the nations of the world and their rulers.

decisions.choice: "이방인들" (L); "민족들" (B); "세상 나라들" (R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the nations of the world and their rulers (meaning decision), not the Romans in particular as in 10:33; Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: gentiles (L); naciones (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the nations of the world and their rulers (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: llamándolos, no bracket
decisions.reason: Spanish "llamar" says "call to himself" without a pronoun, so Literal needs no bracketed word where the English has [Him].

decisions.choice: watu wa mataifa (L); mataifa (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Watu wa mataifa" is the term the Swahili letters use for the Gentiles; here, where the rulers of the nations are meant (meaning decision), Balanced and Readable say simply "mataifa" (the nations).

source.text: οὐχ οὕτως δέ ἐστιν ἐν ὑμῖν· ἀλλ’ ὃς ἂν θέλῃ μέγας γενέσθαι ἐν ὑμῖν, ἔσται ὑμῶν διάκονος, καὶ ὃς ἂν θέλῃ ἐν ὑμῖν εἶναι πρῶτος, ἔσται πάντων δοῦλος·

records.literal_gloss: Not thus however it is among you; but whoever desires great to become among you will be your servant, \v 44 and whoever desires among you to be first will be of all slave.

en.L: But it is not so among you; but whoever wants to become great among you will be your servant, \v 44 and whoever wants to be first among you will be slave of all.
en.B: That is not how it is among you. Instead, whoever among you wants to become great must be your servant, \v 44 and whoever among you wants to be first must serve everyone as a slave.
en.R: But it is not like that with you. If you want to be great, you must serve the others. \v 44 If you want to be first, you must be a slave to everyone.

vi.L: Nhưng giữa các con thì không như vậy; trái lại, ai muốn trở nên lớn giữa các con thì sẽ là người phục vụ các con, \v 44 và ai muốn đứng đầu giữa các con thì sẽ là nô lệ của mọi người.
vi.B: Giữa các con thì không như vậy. Trái lại, ai trong các con muốn làm lớn thì phải làm người phục vụ các con, \v 44 và ai trong các con muốn đứng đầu thì phải làm nô lệ cho mọi người.
vi.R: Nhưng giữa các con thì không như thế. Nếu ai muốn làm lớn, người ấy phải phục vụ những người khác. \v 44 Nếu ai muốn đứng đầu, người ấy phải làm nô lệ cho mọi người.

ko.L: 그러나 너희 가운데서는 그렇지 않다. 오히려 누구든지 너희 가운데서 크게 되고 싶은 사람은 너희를 섬기는 사람이 될 것이다. \v 44 그리고 누구든지 너희 가운데서 첫째가 되고 싶은 사람은 모든 사람의 종이 될 것이다.
ko.B: 그러나 너희는 그렇지 않다. 오히려 너희 가운데서 누구든지 큰 사람이 되고 싶은 사람은 너희를 섬기는 사람이 되어야 한다. \v 44 또 너희 가운데서 누구든지 첫째가 되고 싶은 사람은 모든 사람의 종이 되어야 한다.
ko.R: 그러나 너희는 그래서는 안 된다. 너희 가운데 큰 사람이 되고 싶은 사람은 다른 사람들을 섬겨야 한다. \v 44 너희 가운데 첫째가 되고 싶은 사람은 모든 사람의 종이 되어야 한다.

es.L: Pero no es así entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; sino que el que quiera llegar a ser grande entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} será {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} servidor, \v 44 y el que quiera ser primero entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} será esclavo de todos.
es.B: Entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} no es así. Al contrario, el que entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} quiera ser grande debe ser {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} servidor, \v 44 y el que entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} quiera ser el primero debe servir a todos como esclavo.
es.R: Pero entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} no es así. Si alguno quiere ser grande, tiene que servir a los demás. \v 44 Si alguno quiere ser el primero, tiene que ser esclavo de todos.

fr.L: Mais il n’en est pas ainsi parmi vous ; mais quiconque veut devenir grand parmi vous sera votre serviteur, \v 44 et quiconque veut être le premier parmi vous sera l’esclave de tous.
fr.B: Il n’en est pas ainsi parmi vous. Au contraire, celui qui veut devenir grand parmi vous doit être votre serviteur, \v 44 et celui qui veut être le premier parmi vous doit être l’esclave de tous.
fr.R: Mais chez vous, ce n’est pas comme ça. Si vous voulez être grands, vous devez servir les autres. \v 44 Si vous voulez être les premiers, vous devez être les esclaves de tout le monde.

sw.L: Lakini sivyo ilivyo kati yenu; bali yeyote atakayetaka kuwa mkuu kati yenu, atakuwa mtumishi wenu, \v 44 na yeyote atakayetaka kuwa wa kwanza kati yenu, atakuwa mtumwa wa wote.
sw.B: Lakini kati yenu haiko hivyo. Badala yake, yeyote kati yenu anayetaka kuwa mkuu lazima awe mtumishi wenu, \v 44 na yeyote kati yenu anayetaka kuwa wa kwanza lazima awe mtumwa wa wote.
sw.R: Lakini kwenu ninyi si hivyo. Mtu yeyote kati yenu akitaka kuwa mkuu, lazima awahudumie wengine. \v 44 Akitaka kuwa wa kwanza, lazima awe mtumwa wa kila mtu.

pt.L: Mas entre vocês não é assim; ao contrário, quem quiser se tornar grande entre vocês será servo de vocês, \v 44 e quem quiser ser o primeiro entre vocês será escravo de todos.
pt.B: Entre vocês não é assim. Pelo contrário, quem quiser se tornar grande entre vocês deve ser servo de vocês, \v 44 e quem quiser ser o primeiro entre vocês deve servir a todos como escravo.
pt.R: Mas com vocês não é assim. Se vocês querem ser grandes, precisam servir os outros. \v 44 Se querem ser os primeiros, precisam ser escravos de todos.

decisions.choice: it is not so: a present, the way things are among Jesus' followers
decisions.reason: Jesus states what is true of his community. Some manuscripts have the future "it shall not be", which makes it a command.

decisions.choice: servant: one who waits on others
decisions.reason: The word is the one in 9:35. It is used of those who serve at table.

decisions.choice: slave: one owned by another, with no rights of his own
decisions.reason: The word is stronger than servant. A slave belonged to a master and had no standing. Jesus asks those who would be first to take the lowest place of all.

decisions.choice: will be: a future that works as a command
decisions.reason: As in 9:35, the future states what must be.

decisions.choice: must be
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the force of command.

decisions.choice: If you want to be great
alternatives: whoever wants to become great among you
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to the hearers directly, as in 9:35.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where the word for slave stands against the word for servant in one saying: the step down from servant to slave is the point (m3).

decisions.choice: "người phục vụ" for the servant (diakonos) and "nô lệ" for the slave (doulos), at every level
alternatives: "đầy tớ" for doulos at B, R
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Balanced and Readable say "đầy tớ" for doulos; here the step down from servant to slave is the point, so "nô lệ" stays at every level, as in the English.

decisions.choice: "섬기는 사람" (diakonos) and "종" (doulos), every level
decisions.reason: The step down from one who serves to one who is owned is the point of the saying (as the English rendering decision says). In Korean "섬기는 사람" and "종" already make that step, and "종" is the Korean John's word for doulos (13:16; 15:15); "노예" stays for passages about slavery itself.

decisions.choice: "될 것이다" (L); "되어야 한다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The future works as a command (meaning decision); Literal keeps the future, the other levels say "must".

decisions.choice: servidor
decisions.reason: As in 9:35: "servidor" for one who serves others, kept apart from "esclavo" in the next verse.

decisions.choice: esclavo
decisions.reason: As in English: "slave" set against "servant" in one saying, where the step down is the point; Spanish "siervo" would blur it.

decisions.choice: esclave at every level, set against serviteur
decisions.reason: The French guide follows the English: "esclave" stays at every level where the step down from "servant" to "slave" is the point (meaning decision on slave), as here after "serviteur" in verse 43.

decisions.choice: mtumishi (servant), mtumwa (slave) at every level
decisions.reason: As the English and the Swahili guide: the saying steps down from servant to slave, so "mtumwa" (one owned by another, as the meaning decision says) stays at every level, set against "mtumishi" for the servant.

source.text: καὶ γὰρ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἦλθεν διακονηθῆναι ἀλλὰ διακονῆσαι καὶ δοῦναι τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ λύτρον ἀντὶ πολλῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Even for the Son of Man not came to be served but to serve and to give the life of him a ransom for many.

en.L: For even the Son of Man did not come to be served but to serve, and to give {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life [as] a ransom for many."
en.B: The Son of Man {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} came, not so that others would serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but to serve them and to give {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life as the ransom price for many."
en.R: The Son of Man {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} did not come so that people would serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He came to serve others. He came to give {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life as a ransom, the price paid to set many people free."

vi.L: Vì ngay cả Con Người cũng không đến để được phục vụ, nhưng để phục vụ, và hiến mạng sống mình [làm] giá chuộc cho nhiều người."
vi.B: Chính Con Người đã đến, không phải để được người ta phục vụ, nhưng để phục vụ họ và hiến mạng sống mình làm giá chuộc cho nhiều người."
vi.R: Chính Con Người cũng không đến để được người ta phục vụ. Ngài đến để phục vụ người khác. Ngài đến để hiến mạng sống mình làm giá chuộc, tức là cái giá phải trả để giải phóng nhiều người."

ko.L: 인자도 섬김을 받으러 온 것이 아니라 섬기러 왔고, 많은 사람을 위한 몸값으로 자기 목숨을 주러 왔기 때문이다."
ko.B: 인자도 섬김을 받으러 온 것이 아니라 섬기러 왔고, 많은 사람을 대신하여 그들의 몸값으로 자기 목숨을 내주러 왔다."
ko.R: 인자도 사람들의 섬김을 받으러 오지 않았다. 다른 사람들을 섬기러 왔다. 또 자기 목숨을 몸값으로 내주러 왔다. 그 몸값은 많은 사람을 풀어 주려고 치르는 값이다."

es.L: Porque incluso el Hijo del Hombre no vino a ser servido, sino a servir, y a dar {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} vida [como] rescate por muchos».
es.B: El Hijo del Hombre mismo no vino para que otros {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} sirvieran, sino para servirles a ellos y dar {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} vida como precio de rescate por muchos».
es.R: El Hijo del Hombre mismo no vino para que la gente {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} sirviera. Vino para servir a los demás. Vino a dar {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} vida como rescate, el precio que se paga para dejar libres a muchas personas».

fr.L: Car même le Fils de l’homme n’est pas venu pour être servi, mais pour servir et pour donner {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} vie [en] rançon pour beaucoup. »
fr.B: Le Fils de l’homme {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} est venu, non pour que d’autres {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} servent, mais pour les servir et donner {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} vie comme la rançon payée pour beaucoup. »
fr.R: Le Fils de l’homme {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} n’est pas venu pour que les gens {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} servent. Il est venu pour servir les autres. Il est venu donner {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} vie comme rançon, c’est-à-dire le prix payé pour libérer beaucoup de gens. »

sw.L: Kwa maana hata Mwana wa Adamu hakuja kutumikiwa, bali kutumikia, na kutoa uhai {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} [kuwa] fidia badala ya wengi."
sw.B: Kwa kuwa Mwana wa Adamu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} hakuja ili wengine wamtumikie, bali kuwatumikia na kutoa uhai {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kama gharama ya fidia badala ya wengi."
sw.R: Mwana wa Adamu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} hakuja ili watu wamtumikie. Alikuja kuwatumikia wengine. Alikuja kutoa uhai {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kama fidia, yaani gharama inayolipwa ili watu wengi wawe huru."

pt.L: Pois também o Filho do Homem não veio para ser servido, mas para servir e dar a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} vida [como] resgate por muitos."
pt.B: O próprio Filho do Homem veio, não para que os outros {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} servissem, mas para servi-los e dar a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} vida como o preço do resgate de muitos."
pt.R: O próprio Filho do Homem não veio para que as pessoas {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} servissem. Ele veio para servir os outros. Veio para dar a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} vida como resgate, o preço pago para libertar muitas pessoas."

decisions.choice: ransom: the price paid to set a slave or prisoner free
alternatives: a fee paid to the devil
decisions.reason: The word was used of money paid to free a slave or captive (Leviticus 25:51-52) and of a payment that saved a life that was forfeit (Exodus 21:30; 30:12). Jesus gives his own life as that price. Mark does not say to whom it is paid.

decisions.choice: for: in place of, instead of
decisions.reason: The preposition commonly means in exchange for, or in place of. His life is given in place of theirs.

decisions.choice: many: a great number, set against the one who gives his life
decisions.reason: In Hebrew thought "many" can mean the great multitude, with no thought of leaving others out. The contrast is between the one and the many, as in Isaiah 53:11-12 and Romans 5:15-19.

decisions.choice: to give his life a ransom for many: the suffering servant of Isaiah 53
decisions.reason: Isaiah 53:10-12 says the servant's life is made an offering for sin, that he pours out his life to death and bears the sin of many. Jesus speaks of himself as that servant.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man came to serve: a reversal of Daniel 7:14
decisions.reason: In Daniel 7:13-14 the one like a son of man is given a kingdom, and all peoples serve him. Jesus says the Son of Man came first to serve.

decisions.choice: life: his whole self, his life given up in death
alternatives: his soul as distinct from his body
decisions.reason: The word can mean soul or self; here, as in 8:35, it means a person's life.

decisions.choice: the ransom price
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "price" so that the meaning of ransom is clear.

decisions.choice: a ransom, the price paid to set many people free
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a ransom is in a short added phrase.

decisions.choice: "giá chuộc" for "ransom", at every level
decisions.reason: "giá chuộc" is the price paid to set someone free, without the modern picture of kidnappers' money; Readable explains it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "mạng sống mình" for "his life" (psychē), with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: "mạng sống" is the guide's word for psychē; the reflexive "mình" is the natural Vietnamese and takes no setting span.

decisions.choice: "몸값"
decisions.reason: The ransom is the price paid to set a slave or prisoner free (meaning decision, footnoted); "몸값" is the everyday word for that price. "대속물" is the familiar church word, which a footnote may give.

decisions.choice: "목숨" for psyche
decisions.reason: As in Mark 3:4 and the Korean John: "목숨" is the life a person can give up; "생명" stays for zoe.

decisions.choice: uhai (life); fidia (ransom); badala ya (in place of)
decisions.reason: "Uhai" is life itself, given up in death, which the meaning decision describes; "nafsi" would suggest the soul. "Fidia" is the price paid to free someone. "Badala ya" says "in place of", the sense the meaning decision gives, where "kwa ajili ya" would say only "for the sake of".

decisions.choice: O próprio Filho do Homem
alternatives: O Filho do Homem ele mesmo
decisions.reason: Portuguese stresses the person with "próprio" before the noun, not with a pronoun, so the English span on "himself" has no counterpart. "Resgate" is kept at every level as in Matthew 20:28; Balanced adds "o preço do" as the English adds "price".

source.text: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς Ἰεριχώ.

records.literal_gloss: And they come to Jericho.

en.L: And they come to Jericho.
en.B: Then they came to Jericho.
en.R: Then Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers came to the city of Jericho.

vi.L: Và họ đến Giê-ri-cô.
vi.B: Rồi họ đến Giê-ri-cô.
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu và các môn đồ đến thành Giê-ri-cô.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 여리고에 온다.
ko.B: 그들은 여리고에 이르렀다.
ko.R: 예수와 제자들은 여리고라는 도시에 왔다.

es.L: Y llegan a Jericó.
es.B: Luego llegaron a Jericó.
es.R: Luego Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos llegaron a la ciudad de Jericó.

fr.L: Et ils arrivent à Jéricho.
fr.B: Puis ils arrivèrent à Jéricho.
fr.R: Ensuite, Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples sont arrivés dans la ville de Jéricho.

sw.L: Na wanafika Yeriko.
sw.B: Kisha wakafika Yeriko.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakafika katika mji wa Yeriko.

pt.L: E chegam a Jericó.
pt.B: Então chegaram a Jericó.
pt.R: Então Jesus e os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} seguidores chegaram à cidade de Jericó.

decisions.choice: Jericho: an old city near the Jordan, about fifteen miles from Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Jericho lies in the Jordan valley, far below Jerusalem. Pilgrims from Galilee and Perea passed through it on the steep road up to the city.

decisions.choice: come: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: Jesus and his followers; the city of
decisions.reason: Readable names who came and says what Jericho was.

decisions.choice: "여리고"
decisions.reason: The established Protestant form (style guide, section 5); "예리코" is the Catholic and Common Translation form.

source.text: καὶ ἐκπορευομένου αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ Ἰεριχὼ καὶ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ ὄχλου ἱκανοῦ ὁ υἱὸς Τιμαίου Βαρτιμαῖος τυφλὸς προσαίτης ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν.

records.literal_gloss: And as was going out he from Jericho and the disciples of him and a crowd large, the son of Timaeus Bartimaeus, blind beggar, was sitting beside the road.

en.L: And as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going out from Jericho with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and a large crowd, the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting beside the road.
en.B: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going out of Jericho with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and a large crowd, Bartimaeus son of Timaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting beside the road.
en.R: As Jesus was leaving the city with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers and a big crowd, a blind man was sitting beside the road. He was begging. His name was Bartimaeus, which means son of Timaeus.

vi.L: Và khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cùng các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và một đám đông lớn đang ra khỏi Giê-ri-cô, thì con trai của Ti-mê là Ba-ti-mê, một người mù ăn xin, đang ngồi bên đường.
vi.B: Khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cùng các môn đồ và một đám đông lớn ra khỏi Giê-ri-cô, có một người mù ăn xin là Ba-ti-mê, con trai của Ti-mê, đang ngồi bên vệ đường.
vi.R: Khi Đức Giê-xu cùng các môn đồ và một đám đông lớn rời thành ấy, có một người mù đang ngồi bên vệ đường. Anh ta đang ăn xin. Tên anh là Ba-ti-mê, có nghĩa là con của Ti-mê.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 그분의 제자들과 큰 무리와 함께 여리고를 떠나실 때에, 디매오의 아들 바디매오라는 눈먼 거지가 길가에 앉아 있었다.
ko.B: 예수께서 제자들과 큰 무리와 함께 여리고를 떠나실 때에, 디매오의 아들 바디매오라는 눈먼 거지가 길가에 앉아 있었다.
ko.R: 예수께서 제자들과 많은 사람과 함께 그 도시를 떠나실 때였다. 앞을 보지 못하는 사람 하나가 길가에 앉아 구걸하고 있었다. 그의 이름은 바디매오였는데, 디매오의 아들이라는 뜻이다.

es.L: Y cuando salía de Jericó con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y una gran multitud, el hijo de Timeo, Bartimeo, un mendigo ciego, estaba sentado junto al camino.
es.B: Cuando salía de Jericó con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y una gran multitud, Bartimeo, hijo de Timeo, un mendigo ciego, estaba sentado junto al camino.
es.R: Cuando Jesús salía de la ciudad con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y mucha gente, un hombre ciego estaba sentado junto al camino. Estaba pidiendo limosna. Se llamaba Bartimeo, que quiere decir hijo de Timeo.

fr.L: Et comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sortait de Jéricho avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples et une foule nombreuse, le fils de Timée, Bartimée, un mendiant aveugle, était assis au bord du chemin.
fr.B: Comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sortait de Jéricho avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples et une foule nombreuse, Bartimée, fils de Timée, un mendiant aveugle, était assis au bord de la route.
fr.R: Comme Jésus quittait la ville avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples et une grande foule, un aveugle était assis au bord de la route. Il mendiait. Il s’appelait Bartimée, ce qui veut dire fils de Timée.

sw.L: Na alipokuwa akitoka Yeriko pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} na umati mkubwa, mwana wa Timayo, Bartimayo, kipofu, mwombaji, alikuwa ameketi kando ya njia.
sw.B: Alipokuwa akitoka Yeriko pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} na umati mkubwa wa watu, Bartimayo mwana wa Timayo, kipofu mwombaji, alikuwa ameketi kando ya njia.
sw.R: Yesu alipokuwa akiondoka mjini pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} na umati mkubwa, kipofu mmoja alikuwa ameketi kando ya njia. Alikuwa akiomba msaada. Jina lake lilikuwa Bartimayo, maana yake mwana wa Timayo.

pt.L: E, quando {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} saía de Jericó com os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos e uma grande multidão, o filho de Timeu, Bartimeu, um mendigo cego, estava sentado à beira do caminho.
pt.B: Quando {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} estava saindo de Jericó com os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos e uma grande multidão, Bartimeu, filho de Timeu, um mendigo cego, estava sentado à beira do caminho.
pt.R: Jesus estava saindo da cidade com os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} seguidores e muita gente. Um homem cego estava sentado à beira da estrada. Ele pedia esmolas. O nome dele era Bartimeu, que quer dizer filho de Timeu.

decisions.choice: the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus: the name means son of Timaeus
decisions.reason: Bar is Aramaic for son, so Mark explains the name. He gives the name perhaps because Bartimaeus was known to the first readers.

decisions.choice: a blind beggar by the road: begging from pilgrims on their way to the Passover
alternatives: a man without a home only
decisions.reason: Blind people often had no other way to live than begging. The road out of Jericho was busy with pilgrims going up to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the road: the same word as "the way"
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for Jesus' journey (10:32). At first Bartimaeus sits beside the way; in 10:52 he follows on it.

decisions.choice: which means son of Timaeus
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name in a short sentence.

decisions.choice: "Giê-ri-cô", "Ti-mê", "Ba-ti-mê"
decisions.reason: The Protestant forms of the names, settled for the whole Bible.

decisions.choice: "디매오", "바디매오"; "눈먼" (L, B); "앞을 보지 못하는" (R)
decisions.reason: The established Protestant forms of the names (style guide, section 5). "소경" is now felt as a slur; Readable uses the most respectful plain phrase.

decisions.choice: Bartimée, Timée
decisions.reason: The usual French forms of the two names.

decisions.choice: njia (road, way) at every level
decisions.reason: Swahili "njia" means both the road and the way, so every level keeps the link the meaning decision points to: Bartimaeus sits beside the road and in 10:52 follows Jesus on the way. The English uses "road" and "way" for the one word.

decisions.choice: Bartimayo, Timayo
decisions.reason: The names in the Swahili form of Greek names ending in -aios, as "Zebedayo" in John 21:2.

decisions.choice: Bartimeu, Timeu
decisions.reason: The usual Brazilian forms of the names, as "Zebedeu" and "Alfeu" (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 11).

source.text: καὶ ἀκούσας ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζαρηνός ἐστιν ἤρξατο κράζειν καὶ λέγειν· Υἱὲ Δαυὶδ Ἰησοῦ, ἐλέησόν με.

records.literal_gloss: And having heard that Jesus the Nazarene it is, he began to cry out and to say, Son of David Jesus, have mercy on me.

en.L: And when he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out and say, "Son of David, Jesus, have mercy on me!"
en.B: When he heard it was Jesus of Nazareth, he started to shout, "Son of David, Jesus, have mercy on me!"
en.R: Bartimaeus heard that Jesus from Nazareth was passing by. So he began to shout, "Jesus, Son of David, show mercy to me!"

vi.L: Và khi nghe rằng đó là Đức Giê-xu người Na-xa-rét, anh ta bắt đầu kêu lớn và nói: "Lạy Con của Đa-vít, Đức Giê-xu, xin thương xót tôi!"
vi.B: Khi nghe nói đó là Đức Giê-xu người Na-xa-rét, anh bắt đầu kêu lên: "Lạy Con vua Đa-vít, Đức Giê-xu, xin thương xót tôi!"
vi.R: Ba-ti-mê nghe nói Đức Giê-xu người Na-xa-rét đang đi ngang qua. Vì vậy anh bắt đầu kêu lớn: "Lạy Đức Giê-xu, Con vua Đa-vít, xin thương xót tôi!"

ko.L: 그리고 그가 나사렛 사람 예수라는 말을 듣고 소리 지르며 말하기 시작했다. "다윗의 자손 예수님, 저를 불쌍히 여겨 주십시오!"
ko.B: 그는 나사렛 사람 예수께서 지나가신다는 말을 듣고 소리치기 시작했다. "다윗의 자손 예수님, 저를 불쌍히 여겨 주십시오!"
ko.R: 바디매오는 나사렛에서 오신 예수께서 지나가신다는 말을 들었다. 그래서 큰 소리로 외치기 시작했다. "다윗의 자손 예수님, 저를 불쌍히 여겨 주십시오!"

es.L: Y al oír que era Jesús el Nazareno, comenzó a gritar y a decir: «¡Hijo de David, Jesús, ten misericordia de mí!».
es.B: Cuando oyó que era Jesús de Nazaret, se puso a gritar: «¡Hijo de David, Jesús, ten misericordia de mí!».
es.R: Bartimeo oyó que Jesús de Nazaret estaba pasando. Entonces comenzó a gritar: «¡Jesús, Hijo de David, ten compasión de mí!».

fr.L: Et entendant que c’était Jésus le Nazarénien, il se mit à crier et à dire : « Fils de David, Jésus, aie pitié de moi ! »
fr.B: Quand il entendit que c’était Jésus de Nazareth, il se mit à crier : « Fils de David, Jésus, aie pitié de moi ! »
fr.R: Bartimée a entendu que Jésus de Nazareth passait par là. Alors il s’est mis à crier : « Jésus, Fils de David, aie pitié de moi ! »

sw.L: Na aliposikia kwamba ni Yesu wa Nazareti, alianza kupaza sauti na kusema, "Mwana wa Daudi, Yesu, unihurumie!"
sw.B: Aliposikia kwamba ni Yesu wa Nazareti, alianza kupiga kelele, "Mwana wa Daudi, Yesu, unihurumie!"
sw.R: Bartimayo alisikia kwamba Yesu wa Nazareti alikuwa akipita. Basi akaanza kupiga kelele, "Yesu, Mwana wa Daudi, nionee huruma!"

pt.L: E, ouvindo que era Jesus, o nazareno, começou a gritar e a dizer: "Filho de Davi, Jesus, tem misericórdia de mim!"
pt.B: Quando ouviu que era Jesus de Nazaré, ele começou a gritar: "Filho de Davi, Jesus, tem misericórdia de mim!"
pt.R: Bartimeu ouviu que Jesus de Nazaré estava passando. Por isso começou a gritar: "Jesus, Filho de Davi, tem pena de mim!"

decisions.choice: Son of David: the King God promised from David's family
decisions.reason: God promised David a son whose kingdom would last forever (2 Samuel 7:12-16). By this time "Son of David" was a name for the Messiah. Only here in Mark is Jesus called by it, as he goes up to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: have mercy on me: show me kindness and help me
decisions.reason: The cry asks for pity and help, as people cried to God in the Psalms (Psalm 6:3).

decisions.choice: the Nazarene: the man from Nazareth
decisions.reason: The word names Jesus by his home town, as in 1:24.

decisions.choice: Jesus of Nazareth (B); Jesus from Nazareth (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where the name comes from.

decisions.choice: "Con của Đa-vít" (L); "Con vua Đa-vít" (B, R) for "Son of David"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name David as king so that the title's sense, the King promised from David's family, is heard.

decisions.choice: "Lạy" for the blind man's plea, "tôi" for himself, and "Đức Giê-xu" with the honorific even in his cry
decisions.reason: "Lạy" is the word for a humble plea to one who can help; a bare name would be disrespectful in Vietnamese.

decisions.choice: "다윗의 자손"
decisions.reason: "Son of David" is the title of the king promised from David's family (meaning decision); "자손" (descendant) says that in Korean, where "아들" would suggest David's own son.

decisions.choice: "예수님" in direct address
decisions.reason: A petitioner calls on Jesus respectfully; "님" is the modern honorific of address, where "-여" sounds archaic.

decisions.choice: ten misericordia de mí (L, B); ten compasión de mí (R)
decisions.reason: Readable uses the more everyday word for asking kindness and help (meaning decision). The "mí" is Bartimaeus speaking and takes no setting.

decisions.choice: unihurumie (L, B); nionee huruma (R)
decisions.reason: The blind man asks for kindness and help, as the meaning decision says. "Huruma" is compassion for someone in trouble; "rehema" leans toward God's mercy in pardoning sin, as in Hebrews 2:17 and 4:16.

source.text: καὶ ἐπετίμων αὐτῷ πολλοὶ ἵνα σιωπήσῃ· ὁ δὲ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἔκραζεν· Υἱὲ Δαυίδ, ἐλέησόν με.

records.literal_gloss: And were rebuking him many that he should be silent; but he much more kept crying out, Son of David, have mercy on me.

en.L: And many were rebuking him, [telling him] to be silent; but he kept crying out all the more, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
en.B: Many people scolded him and told him to keep quiet, but he kept shouting even more, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
en.R: Many people told him off and said, "Be quiet!" But he shouted even louder, "Son of David, show mercy to me!"

vi.L: Và nhiều người quở trách anh ta, [bảo anh] im lặng; nhưng anh ta lại càng kêu lớn hơn: "Lạy Con của Đa-vít, xin thương xót tôi!"
vi.B: Nhiều người rầy la, bảo anh im đi, nhưng anh càng kêu lớn hơn nữa: "Lạy Con vua Đa-vít, xin thương xót tôi!"
vi.R: Nhiều người la anh: "Im đi!" Nhưng anh càng kêu to hơn: "Lạy Con vua Đa-vít, xin thương xót tôi!"

ko.L: 그러자 많은 사람이 그를 꾸짖으며 잠잠하라고 [했다]. 그러나 그는 더욱 크게 소리 질렀다. "다윗의 자손이여, 저를 불쌍히 여겨 주십시오!"
ko.B: 많은 사람이 그를 꾸짖으며 조용히 하라고 했다. 그러나 그는 더욱더 크게 소리쳤다. "다윗의 자손이시여, 저를 불쌍히 여겨 주십시오!"
ko.R: 많은 사람이 그를 나무라며 "조용히 해!" 하고 말했다. 그러나 그는 더 큰 소리로 외쳤다. "다윗의 자손이시여, 저를 불쌍히 여겨 주십시오!"

es.L: Y muchos lo reprendían para que callara; pero él gritaba mucho más: «¡Hijo de David, ten misericordia de mí!».
es.B: Muchos lo regañaban y le decían que se callara, pero él gritaba todavía más: «¡Hijo de David, ten misericordia de mí!».
es.R: Mucha gente lo regañó y le dijo: «¡Cállate!». Pero él gritó todavía más fuerte: «¡Hijo de David, ten compasión de mí!».

fr.L: Et beaucoup le réprimandaient pour qu’il se taise ; mais lui criait beaucoup plus : « Fils de David, aie pitié de moi ! »
fr.B: Beaucoup de gens le rabrouaient et lui disaient de se taire, mais il criait encore plus fort : « Fils de David, aie pitié de moi ! »
fr.R: Beaucoup de gens l’ont grondé et lui ont dit : « Tais-toi ! » Mais il a crié encore plus fort : « Fils de David, aie pitié de moi ! »

sw.L: Na wengi wakamkemea ili anyamaze; lakini yeye akazidi sana kupaza sauti, "Mwana wa Daudi, unihurumie!"
sw.B: Watu wengi walimkemea, wakamwambia anyamaze, lakini yeye akazidi kupiga kelele, "Mwana wa Daudi, unihurumie!"
sw.R: Watu wengi wakamkaripia, wakasema, "Nyamaza!" Lakini yeye akapiga kelele kwa nguvu zaidi, "Mwana wa Daudi, nionee huruma!"

pt.L: E muitos o repreendiam para que se calasse; mas ele gritava muito mais: "Filho de Davi, tem misericórdia de mim!"
pt.B: Muita gente o repreendia e mandava que ficasse quieto, mas ele gritava ainda mais: "Filho de Davi, tem misericórdia de mim!"
pt.R: Muitas pessoas brigaram com ele e disseram: "Fique quieto!" Mas ele gritou ainda mais alto: "Filho de Davi, tem pena de mim!"

decisions.choice: were rebuking: sternly telling him to stop
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the disciples with the children (10:13).

decisions.choice: kept crying out all the more: an imperfect, he would not stop
decisions.reason: The tense pictures him shouting again and again, louder each time.

decisions.choice: said, "Be quiet!"
decisions.reason: Readable turns the order into the words spoken.

decisions.choice: [했다]
decisions.reason: The Greek hangs "that he should be silent" on "rebuked"; Korean needs a verb of saying for it, which Literal brackets.

decisions.choice: tem misericórdia (L, B); tem pena (R)
decisions.reason: Bartimaeus calls to Jesus, so he uses the "tu" imperative "tem", as the blind men do in Matthew 20:30; the crowd, speaking to him, says "Fique quieto" with "você".

source.text: καὶ στὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Φωνήσατε αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And having stopped Jesus said, Call him.

en.L: And Jesus stopped and said, "Call him."
en.B: Jesus stood still and said, "Call him over."
en.R: Jesus stopped walking. He said, "Tell him to come here."

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu dừng lại và nói: "Hãy gọi anh ta."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đứng lại và nói: "Hãy gọi anh ấy lại đây."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu dừng bước. Ngài nói: "Hãy bảo anh ấy đến đây."

ko.L: 그러자 예수께서 멈추어 서서 말씀하셨다. "그를 불러라."
ko.B: 예수께서 걸음을 멈추시고 말씀하셨다. "그를 불러오너라."
ko.R: 예수께서 걸음을 멈추셨다. 그리고 말씀하셨다. "그 사람에게 이리 오라고 해라."

es.L: Y deteniéndose, Jesús dijo: «{{plural_you:Llámenlo|Llamadlo}}».
es.B: Jesús se detuvo y dijo: «{{plural_you:Llámenlo|Llamadlo}} para que venga».
es.R: Jesús dejó de caminar. Dijo: «{{plural_you:Díganle|Decidle}} que venga aquí».

fr.L: Et Jésus, s’étant arrêté, dit : « Appelez-le. »
fr.B: Jésus s’arrêta et dit : « Faites-le venir. »
fr.R: Jésus s’est arrêté. Il a dit : « Dites-lui de venir ici. »

sw.L: Na Yesu akasimama, akasema, "Mwiteni."
sw.B: Yesu akasimama, akasema, "Mwiteni aje."
sw.R: Yesu akaacha kutembea, akasema, "Mwambieni aje hapa."

pt.L: E Jesus parou e disse: "Chamem-no."
pt.B: Jesus ficou parado e disse: "Chamem o homem aqui."
pt.R: Jesus parou de andar. Ele disse: "Digam a ele que venha aqui."

decisions.choice: stopped: stood still
decisions.reason: Jesus halts on his way to Jerusalem to answer the cry.

decisions.choice: call: summon
decisions.reason: The verb means to call someone to come. Mark uses it three times in 10:49.

source.text: καὶ φωνοῦσι τὸν τυφλὸν λέγοντες αὐτῷ· Θάρσει, ἔγειρε, φωνεῖ σε.

records.literal_gloss: And they call the blind man saying to him, Take courage, rise up, he calls you.

en.L: And they call the blind man, saying to him, "Take courage, get up; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is calling you."
en.B: So they called to the blind man and told him, "Take courage! Get up! He is calling you."
en.R: So the people called the blind man. They said to him, "It is all right! Get up! Jesus is calling you."

vi.L: Và họ gọi người mù, nói với anh: "Hãy vững lòng, đứng dậy; {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} gọi anh."
vi.B: Vậy họ gọi người mù và bảo anh: "Hãy vững lòng! Đứng dậy đi! Ngài đang gọi anh đó."
vi.R: Vậy người ta gọi người mù. Họ nói với anh: "Không sao đâu! Đứng dậy đi! Đức Giê-xu đang gọi anh đó."

ko.L: 그러자 그들이 그 눈먼 사람을 부르며 그에게 말한다. "용기를 내라. 일어나라. 그분이 너를 부르신다."
ko.B: 사람들이 그 눈먼 사람을 불러 말했다. "용기를 내시오! 일어나시오! 그분께서 당신을 부르십니다."
ko.R: 그래서 사람들이 그 사람을 불렀다. 그리고 말했다. "힘을 내시오! 일어나시오! 예수께서 당신을 부르십니다."

es.L: Y llaman al ciego, diciéndole: «Ánimo, levántate; te llama».
es.B: Entonces llamaron al ciego y le dijeron: «¡Ánimo! ¡Levántate! Te está llamando».
es.R: Entonces la gente llamó al ciego. Le dijeron: «¡Tranquilo! ¡Levántate! Jesús te está llamando».

fr.L: Et ils appellent l’aveugle, lui disant : « Courage, lève-toi ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} t’appelle. »
fr.B: On appela donc l’aveugle en lui disant : « Courage ! Lève-toi ! Il t’appelle. »
fr.R: Alors les gens ont appelé l’aveugle. Ils lui ont dit : « N’aie pas peur ! Lève-toi ! Jésus t’appelle. »

sw.L: Nao wanamwita yule kipofu, wakimwambia, "Jipe moyo, inuka; anakuita."
sw.B: Basi wakamwita yule kipofu, wakamwambia, "Jipe moyo! Simama! Anakuita."
sw.R: Basi watu wakamwita yule kipofu. Wakamwambia, "Usiogope! Simama! Yesu anakuita."

pt.L: E chamam o cego, dizendo-lhe: "Coragem, levante-se; {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} está chamando você."
pt.B: Então chamaram o cego e lhe disseram: "Coragem! Levante-se! Ele está chamando você."
pt.R: Então as pessoas chamaram o cego. Elas disseram a ele: "Está tudo bem! Levante-se! Jesus está chamando você."

decisions.choice: take courage: do not be afraid, be cheerful
decisions.reason: Jesus says the same word to the disciples on the lake (6:50).

decisions.choice: they call: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: they call, he calls: the crowd that silenced him now summons him
decisions.reason: The repeated verb shows the change in the crowd and Jesus' call to the man.

decisions.choice: Jesus is calling you
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.

decisions.choice: "Ngài" for Jesus in the crowd's words (with the setting in the middle of a sentence)
decisions.reason: The people now speak of Jesus with respect, as the English keeps a deity pronoun here; Readable names him.

decisions.choice: the crowd speaks to Bartimaeus in 해라체 (L) and 하오체 with "당신" (B, R), honouring Jesus with "부르신다"
decisions.reason: Strangers addressing a grown man would not use the plain style of a parent to a child; Balanced and Readable use the plain-polite 하오체 that Korean uses between adults in such a scene. Literal keeps the bare imperatives. A native reviewer may prefer another level.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποβαλὼν τὸ ἱμάτιον αὐτοῦ ἀναπηδήσας ἦλθεν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν.

records.literal_gloss: And having cast away the cloak of him, having jumped up he came to Jesus.

en.L: And throwing off his cloak, he jumped up [and] came to Jesus.
en.B: He threw off his cloak, sprang to his feet and came to Jesus.
en.R: Bartimaeus threw his coat to one side, jumped up and went to Jesus.

vi.L: Và anh vứt bỏ áo choàng, nhảy dựng lên, [rồi] đến với Đức Giê-xu.
vi.B: Anh vứt áo choàng lại, đứng phắt dậy và đến với Đức Giê-xu.
vi.R: Ba-ti-mê ném áo khoác sang một bên, nhảy lên và đi đến với Đức Giê-xu.

ko.L: 그러자 그는 자기 겉옷을 벗어 던지고 벌떡 일어나 예수께 왔다.
ko.B: 그는 겉옷을 벗어 던지고 벌떡 일어나 예수께로 갔다.
ko.R: 바디매오는 겉옷을 옆으로 내던지고 벌떡 일어나 예수께 갔다.

es.L: Y él, arrojando su manto, se levantó de un salto [y] fue a Jesús.
es.B: Él arrojó su manto, se puso en pie de un salto y fue hacia Jesús.
es.R: Bartimeo tiró su capa a un lado, se levantó de un salto y fue adonde estaba Jesús.

fr.L: Et ayant jeté son manteau, il bondit [et] vint vers Jésus.
fr.B: Il jeta son manteau, se leva d’un bond et vint vers Jésus.
fr.R: Bartimée a jeté son manteau de côté. Il s’est levé d’un bond et il est allé vers Jésus.

sw.L: Naye akilitupa vazi lake, akaruka juu, akaja kwa Yesu.
sw.B: Akalitupa joho lake, akasimama upesi, akaja kwa Yesu.
sw.R: Bartimayo akalitupa koti lake kando, akaruka juu, akaenda kwa Yesu.

pt.L: E ele, jogando fora a sua capa, deu um salto [e] foi até Jesus.
pt.B: Ele jogou de lado a capa, ficou de pé num salto e foi até Jesus.
pt.R: Bartimeu jogou o casaco para o lado, levantou-se de um pulo e foi até Jesus.

decisions.choice: cloak: the outer garment, a poor man's covering by day and night
decisions.reason: A beggar might spread his cloak to collect coins, and it was his blanket at night (Exodus 22:26-27). He leaves it behind in his eagerness.

decisions.choice: jumped up: leapt to his feet
decisions.reason: The verb shows his eagerness.

decisions.choice: coat
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday word for the outer garment.

decisions.choice: "겉옷"
decisions.reason: The cloak is the outer garment of a poor man, his covering by day and night (meaning decision); "겉옷" is that garment, where "외투" suggests a modern coat.

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Τί σοι θέλεις ποιήσω;

records.literal_gloss: And answering him Jesus said, What for you do you desire I should do?

en.L: And Jesus answered him and said, "What do you want {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?"
en.B: Jesus said to him in reply, "What would you like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?"
en.R: Jesus asked him, "What would you like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?"

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu đáp lời anh và nói: "Anh muốn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm gì cho anh?"
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu hỏi anh: "Anh muốn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm gì cho anh?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu hỏi anh: "Anh muốn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm gì cho anh?"

ko.L: 그러자 예수께서 그에게 대답하여 말씀하셨다. "내가 너에게 무엇을 해 주기를 원하느냐?"
ko.B: 예수께서 그에게 물으셨다. "내가 너에게 무엇을 해 주기를 바라느냐?"
ko.R: 예수께서 그에게 물으셨다. "내가 너에게 무엇을 해 주기를 바라느냐?"

es.L: Y respondiéndole, Jesús dijo: «¿Qué quieres que te haga?».
es.B: Jesús le respondió: «¿Qué quieres que haga por ti?».
es.R: Jesús le preguntó: «¿Qué quieres que haga por ti?».

fr.L: Et prenant la parole, Jésus lui dit : « Que veux-tu que je fasse pour toi ? »
fr.B: Jésus lui répondit : « Que voudrais-tu que je fasse pour toi ? »
fr.R: Jésus lui a demandé : « Qu’est-ce que tu veux que je fasse pour toi ? »

sw.L: Na Yesu akamjibu, akasema, "Unataka nikufanyie nini?"
sw.B: Yesu akamjibu, "Ungependa nikufanyie nini?"
sw.R: Yesu akamwuliza, "Ungependa nikufanyie nini?"

pt.L: E Jesus, respondendo-lhe, disse: "O que você quer que eu lhe faça?"
pt.B: Jesus lhe respondeu: "O que você gostaria que eu fizesse por você?"
pt.R: Jesus perguntou a ele: "O que você gostaria que eu fizesse por você?"

decisions.choice: what do you want me to do for you: the same question as in 10:36
decisions.reason: Jesus asked James and John the same thing. They asked for glory; this man asks for sight.

decisions.choice: answering: speaking in response to the man's cry
decisions.reason: Jesus responds to the man's coming.

decisions.choice: "anh" for "you" when Jesus speaks to Bartimaeus
decisions.reason: The ordinary respectful word for a grown man of no particular rank, as Jesus speaks to the man born blind in John 9.

decisions.choice: the same question as 10:36, word for word
decisions.reason: The meaning decision notes that Jesus asks Bartimaeus the same question he asked James and John; Balanced and Readable keep the two identical so the reader hears the echo.

source.text: ὁ δὲ τυφλὸς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ραββουνι, ἵνα ἀναβλέψω.

records.literal_gloss: And the blind man said to him, Rabbouni, that I may see again.

en.L: And the blind man said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Rabbouni, [I want] to see again."
en.B: The blind man said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Rabbouni, I want to see again."
en.R: The blind man answered, "My Teacher, I want to be able to see again."

vi.L: Và người mù thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ra-bu-ni, [xin cho] tôi được thấy lại."
vi.B: Người mù thưa: "Thưa Ra-bu-ni, xin cho tôi được thấy lại."
vi.R: Người mù trả lời: "Thưa Thầy, tôi muốn được nhìn thấy lại."

ko.L: 그러자 그 눈먼 사람이 그분께 말했다. "랍오니, 다시 보게 [해 주십시오]."
ko.B: 눈먼 사람이 예수께 말했다. "랍오니, 다시 보고 싶습니다."
ko.R: 눈먼 사람이 대답했다. "선생님, 다시 볼 수 있게 해 주십시오."

es.L: Y el ciego {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Rabuni, que recobre la vista».
es.B: El ciego {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Rabuni, quiero volver a ver».
es.R: El ciego respondió: «Maestro mío, quiero poder ver otra vez».

fr.L: Et l’aveugle {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Rabbouni, que je voie de nouveau ! »
fr.B: L’aveugle {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Rabbouni, je veux retrouver la vue. »
fr.R: L’aveugle a répondu : « Mon Maître, je veux pouvoir voir de nouveau. »

sw.L: Na yule kipofu akamwambia, "Rabuni, [nataka] nipate kuona tena."
sw.B: Yule kipofu akamwambia, "Rabuni, nataka kuona tena."
sw.R: Yule kipofu akajibu, "Mwalimu wangu, nataka niweze kuona tena."

pt.L: E o cego {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} disse: "Raboni, [quero] voltar a ver."
pt.B: O cego {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} disse: "Raboni, eu quero voltar a enxergar."
pt.R: O cego respondeu: "Meu Mestre, eu quero poder enxergar de novo."

decisions.choice: Rabbouni: an Aramaic form of Rabbi, my master, my teacher
decisions.reason: The word is a fuller, more personal form of Rabbi. Mary Magdalene uses it of the risen Jesus in John 20:16.

decisions.choice: see again: regain sight, or look up
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to see again, as if he had once been able to see. It can also mean simply to look up or to gain sight.

decisions.choice: that I may see: a request with the main verb left out
decisions.reason: The words mean "I want to see" or "let me see".

decisions.choice: My Teacher
decisions.reason: Readable says what the title means, as it says "Teacher" for Rabbi.

decisions.choice: "Ra-bu-ni" (L, B); "Thưa Thầy" (R)
decisions.reason: As John 20:16; Readable gives the meaning, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "랍오니" (L, B); "선생님" (R)
decisions.reason: "랍오니" is the form of the Korean John (20:16), an Aramaic form of Rabbi (meaning decision); Readable gives its meaning, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: [해 주십시오]
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the main verb out (meaning decision); Korean needs one, and Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: Rabuni (L, B); Maestro mío (R)
decisions.reason: The usual modern Spanish spelling of the Aramaic title; Readable says what it means, as the English does.

decisions.choice: que recobre la vista, no bracket
decisions.reason: A Spanish "que" with the subjunctive can stand alone as a request, just as the Greek does, so Literal needs no bracketed verb.

decisions.choice: que je voie de nouveau ! (L), with no bracketed words
decisions.reason: French "que" with the subjunctive expresses a wish with the main verb left out, as the Greek does (meaning decision), so Literal needs no supplied words where the English brackets "I want".

decisions.choice: Rabuni (L, B); Mwalimu wangu (R)
decisions.reason: "Rabuni" is the form used in Swahili John 20:16 for the same Aramaic title; Readable says what it means, "my Teacher", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Raboni
decisions.reason: The Aramaic title in the spelling Brazilian readers know from John 20:16; Readable says what it means, "Meu Mestre", as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ὕπαγε, ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε.

records.literal_gloss: And Jesus said to him, Go, the faith of you has saved you.

en.L: And Jesus said to him, "Go; your faith has saved you."
en.B: Jesus told him, "Go. Your faith has saved you and made you well."
en.R: Jesus said to him, "Go. Your faith has made you well and saved you."

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu nói với anh: "Hãy đi; đức tin của anh đã cứu anh."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu bảo anh: "Hãy đi. Đức tin của anh đã cứu anh và chữa lành cho anh."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với anh: "Hãy đi. Đức tin của anh đã chữa lành anh và cứu anh."

ko.L: 그러자 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "가거라. 네 믿음이 너를 구원하였다."
ko.B: 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "가거라. 네 믿음이 너를 구원하였고 너를 낫게 하였다."
ko.R: 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "가거라. 네 믿음이 너를 낫게 하였고 너를 구원하였다."

es.L: Y Jesús le dijo: «Vete, tu fe te ha salvado».
es.B: Jesús le dijo: «Vete. Tu fe te ha salvado y te ha sanado».
es.R: Jesús le dijo: «Vete. Tu fe te ha sanado y te ha salvado».

fr.L: Et Jésus lui dit : « Va ; ta foi t’a sauvé. »
fr.B: Jésus lui dit : « Va. Ta foi t’a sauvé et guéri. »
fr.R: Jésus lui a dit : « Va. Ta foi t’a guéri et sauvé. »

sw.L: Naye Yesu akamwambia, "Nenda; imani yako imekuokoa."
sw.B: Yesu akamwambia, "Nenda. Imani yako imekuokoa na kukuponya."
sw.R: Yesu akamwambia, "Nenda. Imani yako imekuponya na kukuokoa."

pt.L: E Jesus lhe disse: "Vá; a sua fé o salvou."
pt.B: Jesus lhe disse: "Vá. A sua fé o salvou e o curou."
pt.R: Jesus disse a ele: "Vá. A sua fé curou você e salvou você."

decisions.choice: has saved: has made well, and more
decisions.reason: The verb means both healing and rescue by God, as in 5:34. The man's sight is restored, and he follows Jesus on the way.

decisions.choice: faith: trust in Jesus to help him
decisions.reason: His faith was shown in his crying out and coming to Jesus. Jesus credits his faith, as he did the woman's in 5:34.

decisions.choice: go: you are free to go
decisions.reason: Jesus sends him on his way healed. He chooses to follow Jesus instead.

decisions.choice: saved you and made you well (B); made you well and saved you (R)
decisions.reason: As at 5:34, Balanced and Readable give both senses of the verb: the healing and the saving.

decisions.choice: "đức tin" for faith, at every level
decisions.reason: The key term keeps one word at every level, as in Colossians.

decisions.choice: "믿음"; "구원하다" with "낫게 하다" added at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: "Faith" is a key term, "믿음" at every level. The verb means both made well and saved (meaning decision, footnoted); Balanced and Readable give both, as the English does.

decisions.choice: kuokoa (L); kuokoa na kuponya (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Kuokoa" (save) keeps the Greek word, which the meaning decision says means made well and more; Balanced and Readable add "kuponya" (heal), as the English adds "made you well".

source.text: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀνέβλεψεν, καὶ ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately he received sight and he was following him on the road.

en.L: And immediately he saw again, and he was following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on the way.
en.B: At once his sight came back, and he followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} along the road.
en.R: Right away the man could see again. He went with Jesus along the road and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

vi.L: Và lập tức anh thấy lại được, và đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trên đường.
vi.B: Ngay lúc đó anh thấy lại được, và anh đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trên đường.
vi.R: Ngay lập tức anh nhìn thấy lại được. Anh cùng đi với Đức Giê-xu trên đường và theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 그는 곧 다시 보게 되었고, 길에서 그분을 따라가고 있었다.
ko.B: 그러자 곧바로 그는 다시 보게 되었고, 길을 따라 예수를 따라갔다.
ko.R: 그 사람은 바로 다시 볼 수 있게 되었다. 그리고 예수와 함께 길을 가며 예수를 따랐다.

es.L: Y enseguida recobró la vista, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} seguía en el camino.
es.B: Al instante recobró la vista, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguió por el camino.
es.R: Enseguida el hombre pudo ver otra vez. Se fue con Jesús por el camino y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguió.

fr.L: Et aussitôt il vit de nouveau, et il {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivait sur le chemin.
fr.B: Aussitôt il retrouva la vue, et il {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivit sur la route.
fr.R: Tout de suite, l’homme a pu voir de nouveau. Il est parti avec Jésus sur la route et il {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a suivi.

sw.L: Na mara moja akapata kuona tena, akawa akimfuata njiani.
sw.B: Mara moja aliweza kuona tena, akamfuata njiani.
sw.R: Mara moja yule mtu aliweza kuona tena. Akaenda pamoja na Yesu njiani, akimfuata.

pt.L: E imediatamente voltou a ver e {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} seguia no caminho.
pt.B: Na mesma hora ele recuperou a vista e {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} seguiu pela estrada.
pt.R: Logo o homem conseguiu enxergar de novo. Ele foi com Jesus pela estrada e {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} seguiu.

decisions.choice: following him on the way: he becomes a disciple on the road to Jerusalem
alternatives: he walked behind for a while
decisions.reason: "Follow" is Mark's word for discipleship (1:18; 8:34), and "the way" is the road to Jerusalem and the cross (10:32). The healed man goes where Jesus goes.

decisions.choice: he saw again: a sight that the disciples still lack
decisions.reason: As with the blind man of 8:22-26, the healing closes a section in which the disciples fail to see what Jesus is teaching about his death.

decisions.choice: was following: an imperfect, he went on following
decisions.reason: The tense shows a continuing action.

decisions.choice: on the way (L); along the road (B, R)
alternatives: on the way at every level
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word that can also mean the way of discipleship. Balanced and Readable describe the road.

decisions.choice: "곧" (L); "곧바로" (B); "바로" (R) for euthys
decisions.reason: As in chapters 3 and 9.
